Vanuatu files ICJ case seeking sovereignty over French-controlled Pacific islands. Mexican soldiers kill suspected cartel hitman. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. launches strikes on southern Iran, killing 18: The U.S. expanded its strikes into southern Iran, killing 18 people, Iranian media reported on Wednesday. Island regions: The U.S. struck several villages on Iran's Qeshm Island, hitting a fish powder factory, and also hit Lavan Island, killing three members of the paramilitary Basij force. Hormozgan: A U.S. attack a wedding in Sirik on Tuesday, killing at least four people, including a child, and injuring nearly 100 people, 51 of whom were hospitalized, to Iran's Health Ministry. Separate U.S. strikes hit a fishing pier and a port authority tower in the city. The U.S. also struck the major southern port city of Bandar Abbas, the city of Jask, and a residential area in the coastal city of Kuhestak. Several parts of the power grid in Hormozgan were also targeted. Kermanshah: The U.S. killed four Iranian military personnel in an overnight attack on the western province of Kermanshah, according to a statement from Iran's military. Sistan and Baluchestan: The U.S. struck the port city of Chabahar several times on Tuesday, and hit the nearby city of Konarak as well. Khuzestan: A U.S. missile struck the outskirts of the Iranian city of Ahvaz, in the country's western Khuzestan province, Iran's Fars news agency reported, and later strikes hit at least two other locations. Tuesday strikes killed at least seven and injured eight others in the province. Kerman: The U.S. also targeted an airport in the city of Jirfot, in Iran's southeast, Iranian broadcaster IRIB reported, though the attack entailed no casualties and minimal damage to the airport's infrastructure. Bushehr: Explosions were also heard in the gas hub of Asaluyeh. Markazi: Iranian forces shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone over Khomeyn, in central Iran on Tuesday, Tasnim reported. Iran launches retaliatory attacks: Iranian officials announced that the country would launch "regretful" retaliatory attacks on Tuesday, with a spokesman for the IRGC saying the U.S. would face "severe punishment" for its latest attack on Iran. Jordan: Iran launched several rockets towards Jordan, claiming a successful strike on the U.S. military barracks at Camp Titin, near the Gulf of Aqaba. Iran claimed it killed several U.S. forces and destroyed "several installations and enemy attack helicopters" at the base, while a U.S. source told Al Jazeera the attack had not caused any injuries or major damage. Iran also claimed a successful ballistic missile strike on a helicopter hangar at the Prince Hassan Base in Jordan, and launched attacks at the city of Mafraq. Jordanian officials claimed that they intercepted 10 of 13 Iranian missiles launched into the kingdom, that the remaining three landed in remote areas, and that no injuries or deaths were recorded. Bahrain: Iran launched drone attacks on U.S. forces in Bahrain, at the country's Sheikh Isa Airbase, according to a statement issued by Iran's Tasnim news service. Bahrain's Ministry of Interior later reported several missile interceptions over its airspace. Kuwait: The Kuwaiti army reported that the country's air defenses were responding to attacks by "hostile," Iran-linked drones in its airspace. Kuwait's fire service later said a fire at a residential complex in the capital was brought under control after an alleged Iranian drone strike with no injuries reported. Iran claimed its attack on Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem airbase inflicted casualties. Iraq: Iran's IRGC said its forces carried out a combined missile and drone attack on U.S. facilities in Erbil province, northern Iraq, killing several U.S. personnel, destroying a repair center and warehouses containing technical equipment. Its claims of casualties and damage have not been independently verified. Syria : Three missiles aimed at Jordan were intercepted over the eastern Deraa countryside in southern Syria, Al Jazeera reported on Tuesday evening. United Arab Emirates: Iran said it struck radar stations at the Al-Dhafra and Al-Minhad bases in the UAE on Wednesday. The UAE did not confirm the attacks. IRGC says two oil tankers hit Hormuz mines and were disabled: The IRGC said two oil tankers hit sea mines and were disabled while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to a statement shared on Iranian state media. The IRGC claimed that the tankers had attempted a transit through the "illegal" southern route with the help of U.S. operatives, and that they were forced to disembark their crews. CENTCOM claims 84 vessels redirected during naval blockade: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said as of Tuesday evening, U.S. forces had redirected 84 commercial vessels during its ongoing naval blockade against Iran, adding one vessel redirection to Sunday's toll. In a on X, CENTCOM added that it had disabled three vessels and boarded two to "ensure compliance." Trump threatens to escalate attacks, says Gulf allies privy to latest wave of U.S. attacks: President Donald Trump threatened on Tuesday evening to U.S. attacks on Iran if Tehran retaliated, telling Fox News: "They'll be hit much harder...if it goes a third time, they're going to be totally wiped out as a country." He had earlier in a Truth Social post that the "biggest attack of them all" was "waiting in the wings," should Iran respond to the latest wave of attacks Separately, Trump said that the U.S. had "almost total control" of Hormuz on Tuesday, and dismissed reports that the U.S. was seeking a new agreement with Iran. Trump also claimed in his Fox News interview that the U.S.'s Gulf allies were notified before the latest round of U.S. strikes on Iran. Head of Iran 's Supreme National Security Council vows retaliation: In response to the U.S. attacks, Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said in a : "You will soon see that Iran's new strategy on the battlefield, in diplomacy, and in confronting the economic blockade will shatter your foundations." Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei called the U.S. bombing of a wedding a "war crime" and said in a on X: "The truth of America's illegal war against Iran was revealed last night in #Sirik; where a wedding ceremony was bombed, within the framework of America's desperate attempt to conceal its own defeat; the reality is the crimes that America commits, not the AI-generated videos that falsely depict American officials as morally upright and victorious heroes." Russia affirms solidarity with Iran, Putin tells Pezeshkian: President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization meeting on Tuesday that Russia stood in solidarity with the Iranian people. Putin also told Pezeshkian that Russia and Iran would maintain their economic and trade relationship despite U.S. threats against countries that cooperate with Iran. Ghalibaf claims U.S. giving ships "false guarantees" about Hormuz passage: In a video message shared by Iranian news agencies, parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf addressed the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, saying that, despite a few "enemy" ships managing to get through the passageway, Iranian forces remained "in complete control" of the Strait and would "not allow it to be opened. He claimed the U.S. was giving ships "false guarantees" about their ability to cross a southern route in Hormuz, adding that ships that try to do so are being targeted. In his remarks, Ghalibaf also threatened that "no one" would be "able to export oil," should the U.S.'s stranglehold on Iranian oil continue. U.S. previews more sanctions on Iranian business partners: At the G20 finance meeting on Tuesday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the U.S. planned to announce new sanctions on "anyone that does business with the IRGC." He also claimed that the U.S. was presently tracking down the group's assets. Saudi shipping firm says two sailors killed in Hormuz transit: The Saudi shipping company Bahri reported on Wednesday that two Filipino crew members were killed on board the Sidr supertanker in a Monday incident in the Strait of Hormuz. Peru cuts diplomatic ties with Iran: Peru announced on Tuesday that it had severed diplomatic relations with Iran, accusing Iran of "inciting violence" and "escalating" the conflict in the Middle East, and citing disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in a statement from its Foreign Ministry. The two countries have had diplomatic relations since November 1973. USS Abraham Lincoln arrives in Thailand after more than 6 months at sea: After more than 200 consecutive days at sea, the U.S. Navy aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln arrived in Thailand on Wednesday, Reuters reported. The vessel plans to dock in the Southeast Asian country for five days. The vessel has been plagued by reports of deteriorating conditions on board and concerns over the mental health of some sailors and marines after its long deployment. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 31 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One Palestinian was killed in a building collapse, bringing the number of people killed in building collapses to 34. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,470 killed, with 174,540 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,334 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,429, while 815 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks kill Palestinian boy in Jabalia, woman dies of wounds in Deir al-Balah: A Palestinian boy was and another person wounded in an Israeli strike on the Al-Hawja area of Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza on Wednesday, according to WAFA. In central Gaza, a 51-year-old woman died from wounds sustained from Israeli forces a day earlier. " Why should a child filling up water die?": An Israeli attack in the Al-Katiba area of western Gaza City killed four, including two children and a woman, and wounded eight, on Tuesday. Families had gathered to collect water in the area. "The water tanker came, and we started filling up water, us and our children," Faiza Al-Bahtini, the aunt of one of the children killed, told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed. "Then we heard gunfire coming from every direction. After that, the vehicles came, the Israelis started bombing, and the massacre happened." The Israeli military claimed it was targeting the head of Hamas's internal security apparatus in Gaza and strikes were carried out to "remove threats." Abu al-Abd, an eyewitness who was filling water with his four children, said: "What is the crime of a child filling up water? ... Because a child was filling up water, Netanyahu shot at him. What have these children done to you?" Watch Ahmed 's dispatch . Netanyahu visits Gaza, vows no withdrawal: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited an Israeli military post near the "yellow line" in Gaza on Wednesday. In a on X alongside a Hebrew-language video, Netanyahu said, "Today we control the area and we are holding this line. We have more work to complete and we will complete it--until Hamas is disarmed and Gaza is demilitarized. Gaza will no longer pose a threat to Israel!" Israeli demolitions, land razing, detentions and settler attacks continue across occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces around 10 structures in the village of Al-Tabban in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, on Wednesday, including tin homes, barracks, sheep pens, and water wells, WAFA reported. Residents were prevented from removing their belongings before the demolitions began. Salfit: Israeli forces Deir Ballut Mayor and three other Palestinians while they were on agricultural land west of the town on Wednesday. Israeli bulldozers have been razing land and uprooting hundreds of olive trees in the area for four consecutive days to build a settlement road. Jenin: Israeli forces continued razing agricultural land and uprooting trees in Arraba, southwest of Jenin, for a second consecutive day on Wednesday. Arraba Mayor said around 223 dunams (55 acres) are currently being bulldozed. Nablus: Israeli settlers the eastern area of Beita, south of Nablus, early Wednesday and set fire to two Palestinian vehicles parked outside homes. East Jerusalem: Israeli authorities a three-story residential building in the Al-Bustan neighborhood of Silwan, on Wednesday. The approximately 500-square-meter building contained four homes. Palestinian ministry documents pattern of Israeli restrictions on Islamic holy sites in August: Israel restrictions on Islamic holy sites in August, with 26 incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque and the call to prayer blocked 155 times at Hebron's Ibrahimi Mosque, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Awqaf. The ministry also documented restrictions on worshippers, settler incursions at Al-Aqsa, and attacks on mosques and Islamic shrines elsewhere in the occupied West Bank. Hamas condemns Israeli attacks on Gaza in talks with mediators, Mladenov: Hamas said on Wednesday it held talks with mediators and "Board of Peace" High Representative Nickolay Mladenov, condemning Israeli attacks on Gaza that killed and wounded Palestinians. The group urged ceasefire mediators and guarantors to "exert the utmost pressure" on the Israeli government to halt its attacks, saying Israel is taking "deliberate escalatory steps" aimed at undermining the ceasefire and efforts to complete its implementation. WHO: Water contamination nearly triples in Gaza as rainy season threatens public health crisis: The World Health Organization on Tuesday that the approaching rainy season could worsen Gaza's public health crisis, with flooding threatening to spread sewage, waste and contaminated water through overcrowded displacement camps. Microbiological contamination in tested water samples nearly tripled this year, while cases of acute watery diarrhoea rose from about 27,000 in March to more than 48,000 in August. The organization called for the "unimpeded and expedited entry of humanitarian supplies" to prevent a further deterioration, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of life essentials into Gaza. U.S. claims it seized more than $560,000 in cryptocurrency donations intended for Hamas: The U.S. Justice Department on Wednesday that the FBI seized more than $560,000 in cryptocurrency donations it claimed was intended for Hamas. It also said authorities took control of web domains and communication platforms allegedly used for fundraising and recruitment, and obtained information on thousands of people it says had contacted Hamas seeking to donate money. East Jerusalem teachers strike as Israel imposes curriculum, blocks teacher permits : Teachers at private and Christian schools in occupied East Jerusalem launched an open-ended strike Tuesday as the academic year began, protesting Israel's requirement that all new first and seventh-grade classes at Palestinian-majority municipal schools use the Israeli curriculum exclusively, according to Al Jazeera. The change will affect more than 45,000 students, or one in three Palestinian students in the city. Israel has also blocked entry permits for more than 70 West Bank teachers and staff without warning, according to the General Secretariat for Christian Educational Institutions in Jerusalem, which called the abrupt reversal "unprecedented." A Knesset law passed earlier this year barring employment of teachers with Palestinian Authority degrees compounds the crisis, since about 60% of East Jerusalem's Arab educators hold such degrees. Lebanon Israeli attacks kill one, wound another in southern Lebanon as ceasefire violations continue: Israeli attacks across southern Lebanon on Wednesday one person and wounded another in Nabatieh, where a drone struck the Al-Ruwais neighborhood, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli drones also struck the Al-Deir and Al-Maslah neighborhoods of Nabatieh, including an apartment hit by a guided missile. Israeli forces also a large explosion in Kfar Tebnit, as well as explosions near Mansouri and Majdal Zoun in the Tyre district and in Houla. Israeli attacks continue to displace Lebanese residents of the south, with UNHCR spokesperson telling the Anadolu News Agency that "more than 350,000 people remain displaced across Lebanon while approximately 860,000 people have returned to their communities of origin or nearby areas although many continue to face significant challenges and these should not be considered durable returns." Around 23,000 people remain in shelters. EU plans new mission to train Lebanese army as UNIFIL mandate nears end: The European Union is planning a new mission to advise and train Lebanese soldiers, including on border and maritime security, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Wednesday. "We are investing in Lebanon's capacity to provide security for itself," Kallas said, stressing that the mission would not replace UNIFIL, whose mandate expires on December 31 after 48 years. The EU aims for a decision to launch the mission in October. U.S. News Ed Markey wins Massachusetts Democratic Senate Primary: Democratic Sen. Ed Markey easily defeated Rep. Seth Moulton in Massachusetts' Senate primary, winning about two-thirds of the vote despite being outspent on ads by more than $3 million. Markey, 80, campaigned on his liberal record as an author of the Green New Deal and supporter of "Medicare for All," touting endorsements from Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , while attacking Moulton's past criticism of the party's left flank and his previous comments about transgender athletes. Hegseth 's military purge tops 80 generals and admirals: War Secretary Pete Hegseth has or blocked the promotions of more than 80 generals and admirals, roughly 10% of the military's top officers, according to The New York Times. In the past week, Hegseth has removed seven Army officers selected for two-star general rank, two of whom are black and two of whom are female. Army SecretaryDaniel P. Driscoll recently resigned in protest, warning President Donald Trump directly that the firings have imperiled Army modernization and damaged morale by undermining faith in a promotion system meant to be apolitical. Top Pentagon AI official sells AI company stake for millions: Emil Michael , the Pentagon's top official overseeing military AI policy, his holdings in AI search engine Perplexity for between $5 million and $25 million in June, according to financial disclosures reviewed by the Guardian, following an earlier disclosed sale of his stake in Elon Musk 's xAI that netted gains of between 400% and 4,800%. Michael also sold holdings in financial software firm Brex, backed by Peter Thiel and recently acquired by Capital One, for at least $5 million in April, a gain of at least 473% from the $750,000 maximum value he reported in March 2025. Michael, who previously served as Uber's chief business officer, received a personal loan from Perplexity in 2025 and sat on its advisory board before stepping down upon entering federal service. Two House Democrats break ranks to save GOP procedural vote: Democratic Reps. Jared Golden of Maine and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington the necessary votes on Tuesday to advance a key GOP procedural vote, stalled by five Republican defections, which set up votes on several GOP-led bills, including a controversial resolution condemning socialism. Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez said they supported the measure because it enabled passage of a bill pushed by Golden which would delay fishing regulations and potentially benefit Maine lobstermen. That bill later passed 219-196. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Minority Whip Katherine Clark both said they were not given advance notice of Golden and Gluenskamp Perez's votes. Chinese immigrant found dead hours after entering ICE custody: Lianyong Wei , a 51-year-old Chinese immigrant, was unresponsive during morning checks and pronounced dead on August 23, less than a day after being taken into ICE custody at a facility in the Northern Mariana Islands. His cause of death remains under investigation. Wei, whose legal status had ended in 2019, had been arrested by local police on August 21 after allegedly attacking a family in their home. Wei's death is the 57th of an immigrant in ICE custody since the start of Trump's second term, 24 of which have occurred since January 1. State Department proposes requiring parents to prove citizenship for children 's passports: The State Department has requiring parents applying for their children's passports to provide proof of their own citizenship or immigration status as part of President Donald Trump's latest effort to limit birthright citizenship, according to draft guidance reviewed by Reuters. Under the proposal, parents of applicants would need to submit documents such as a valid U.S. passport, birth certificate, or immigration papers like an I-94 form or green card. The proposal follows an August 6 executive order targeting "birth tourism," following an earlier executive order limiting U.S. citizenship to children of green card holders, which the Supreme Court found to be unlawful. ICE arrests hold near record high with roughly 50,000 in August : ICE officers and agents approximately 50,000 people in August, roughly matching July's record total, NBC News reported, citing a senior Department of Homeland Security official familiar with preliminary data. The toll has continued rising since May after a sharp drop in February and March, with June and July both setting arrest records. The buildup is fueled by a roughly $70 billion funding package Republicans narrowly passed through the House in June, making ICE the wealthiest law enforcement agency in American history. With that funding, the agency has announced that it will purchase "turnkey" detention facilities and controversial new tools, including electric gloves and robot dogs. Mullin says ICE could deploy to polling sites for "specific threats": Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin Tuesday that ICE could enter polling places to serve warrants on tracked individuals or respond to "specific threats." He maintained that ICE would not "patrol polling places." A DHS statement echoed Mullin, saying "ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations" but that agents conducting "intelligence-driven targeted enforcement" could make arrests at a location if "an active public safety threat" were present there. Tuesday's comments follow Mullin's comments in July, in which he claimed that immigration agents were reviewing state voter rolls "looking for illegal aliens and those who are ineligible to vote." DOJ sues Kansas City schools over gender policy, first such federal action : The Justice Department Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools Tuesday, accusing the district of facilitating "secret transition" of students' gender without parental knowledge, marking the first federal lawsuit against a public school district over gender identity policy. The suit alleges that the district violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment by not requiring parental consent before discussing gender identity or changing students' names and pronouns. The lawsuit comes nearly six months after the Supreme Court ruled to temporarily suspend policies in California that allowed public school teachers to avoid outing transgender students to their parents. Federal judge strikes down New York 's climate "superfund" law: Judge Brenda K. Sannes of the Northern District of New York ruled Monday that New York's 2024 climate superfund law, which required large fossil fuel companies to pay $75 billion over 25 years for climate resilience projects, is unenforceable, finding it conflicts with federal law. Sannes, an Obama appointee, relied heavily on a 2021 Second Circuit ruling dismissing a similar New York City lawsuit against oil companies. Several Republican-led states, including West Virginia, had argued that the law was illegal, and that only the federal government has the authority to regulate greenhouse gases. Tyson lays off 2,500 workers overnight in abrupt Illinois plant closure : Tyson Foods abruptly shuttered its beef plant in Joslin, Illinois on August 14, laying off 2,500 workers, mostly immigrants from Africa, Latin America. Tyson claimed that it closed the facility in response to a nationwide cattle shortage, driven partly by drought and the Iran war's effect on fertilizer and diesel costs. Tyson's operating income, however, rose 8%, or $547 million, over the past year and its CEO, Donnie King , earned nearly $35 million last year, 781 times the median worker's pay. UFCW Local 1546, which represents the workers, said it was not given advance notice. Its leadership later signed a severance agreement providing one to four weeks of pay on top of two months of wage continuation, an agreement criticized by several workers. More on the Joslin plant closure, and the union response to it, is available from Labor Notes . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Global warming set to exceed 1.5 °C within years, UN warns: The world is likely to the Paris Agreement's key 1.5°C warming threshold within the next few years, intensifying extreme weather and threats to ecosystems, glaciers and low-lying coastal cities, according to the UN Environment Programme. With an "overshoot" now extremely likely, governments must focus on limiting how far and how long temperatures remain above 1.5°C. UNEP said returning temperatures below the threshold remains possible but "highly uncertain." Even if every existing national climate pledge is implemented, warming is projected to peak at approximately 1.8°C above preindustrial levels. Under current government policies, median warming is projected to reach roughly 2.6°C by 2100. U.S. won 't negotiate on commerce, diplomacy with Cuba: The Trump administration won't commerce, diplomacy, or any other issue that could ease the suffering caused by U.S. sanctions, Cuban officials told Bloomberg on Tuesday. "The channel for dialogue is at a complete standstill," said Lianys Torres Rivera, Cuba's top diplomat in Washington. The two sides cannot even agree on an agenda. "There are no negotiations." Meanwhile, President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are tightening economic pressure to force Cuba's leaders from power, including through a de facto fuel blockade, as the island faces rising infant mortality and preventable deaths. Chinese president calls for new Middle East security order during Egypt visit: Chinese President Xi Jinping Middle Eastern countries to oppose external interference and become "masters of their own destiny" during talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo on Wednesday that also saw the signing of numerous bilateral economic deals. Xi said China was prepared to work with regional countries to safeguard shipping routes following disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb. China and Egypt agreed to deepen security cooperation and counterterrorism coordination. The two countries also agreed to expand cooperation on data centers, semiconductors and critical-minerals supply chains and increase the use of their currencies in bilateral trade. Egypt's Suez Canal Economic Zone has already attracted around $4 billion in Chinese investment. Germany accuses Russia of drone attack on Leipzig airport, expels diplomats: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt Tuesday that investigators found proof Russian agents controlled the explosive-laden drone found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig-Halle Airport on August 4, calling it part of "a broader pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe." In response, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said the country would summon its Russian ambassador, close Russia's consulate general in Bonn and the Russian House cultural center in Berlin, and push for additional EU sanctions and travel restrictions on Russian nationals. Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected the accusations at the SCO summit in Bishkek, calling Germany's response a "serious mistake" and suggesting Berlin had "fabricated" the evidence. European and NATO leaders quickly backed Germany, with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte saying the evidence was "clear", and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announcing that EU foreign ministers would prepare additional sanctions at an upcoming meeting. Germany investigates second power-grid sabotage attempt in 24 hours: German police are apparent deliberate damage to a power substation near Bergheim in western Germany, the second suspected attack on the country's electricity grid within a day. The incident followed an attack on a critical high-voltage node in Brandenburg, where devices carrying conductive material damaged power lines. The attacks came after Berlin accused Russia of attempting to use drones to strike a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle airport last month. Moscow denied involvement, while EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas said the incident bore "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." German officials described the timing as "extremely suspicious" ahead of this weekend's Saxony-Anhalt election. South Korean president calls for revival of U.S.-North Korea dialogue: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said conditions should be for Washington and Pyongyang to resume talks and called for replacing the Korean Peninsula's armistice system with a permanent peace framework. Lee also pledged to complete the transfer of wartime operational control of South Korean forces from the United States before his term ends in 2030. South Korea's intelligence agency said this week that North Korea and the United States were showing signs of preparing to resume dialogue, although no direct contacts have been confirmed. Vanuatu files ICJ case seeking sovereignty over French-controlled Pacific islands: Vanuatu an application with the International Court of Justice on Tuesday, seeking sovereignty over Matthew Island and Hunter Island, two uninhabited volcanic islands currently controlled by France. The case, which will not proceed unless France consents to the court's jurisdiction, seeks to resolve a decades-old dispute rooted in the area's colonial past. Vanuatu argues its decolonization from joint French-British rule, which ended in 1980, remains incomplete without the islands' return. Vanuatu and France have had two previous rounds of bilateral negotiations over the islands, and agreed to a third round in 2026. The islands are located about 300 kilometers from French-controlled New Caledonia, and include significant fishing rights and access to seabed resources. Mexican soldiers kill suspected cartel hitman : Mexican soldiers Luis Enrique Barragan Chavez, a suspected top hitman for the Los Reyes cartel faction of the Carteles Unidos criminal group during an operation in Michoacan on Tuesday, according to Mexico's defense ministry. The U.S. had offered a $3 million reward for information leading to Barragan's arrest and had indicted him on drug conspiracy and firearms charges. | | Dear Fellow American, For decades, Planned Parenthood has staked its business on taking lives. Thanks to the billions of dollars it's received from the government via taxpayers--including your--it's the nation's largest abortion business. **According to a _New York Times_ expose, Planned Parenthood's single-minded focus on abortion has led to serious problems at its facilities:**
* Some are filthy, staff are untrained, and sometimes care leaves women injured and scarred--physically and emotionally.
* One woman reported that her failed abortion resulted in weeks of pain, bleeding, and eventually an emergency delivery of a baby who later died.
* Many Planned Parenthood facilities have fallen into disrepair. In one, sewage seeped into the abortion recovery room for days, making patients physically ill.

**These stories make my stomach turn.** And, unfortunately, it doesn't stop there. Planned Parenthood's track record of distributing dangerous "gender-transition" drugs is equally disturbing. Planned Parenthood has become the nation's _second-largest distributor of "gender-transition" drugs._ It boasts about giving these drugs to minors. Think about that: Planned Parenthood profits from giving vulnerable, confused, and hurting kids drugs that can permanently damage their bodies. And I haven't even mentioned the organization's devastating legacy of racism and eugenics. Needless to say, Planned Parenthood has been riddled with scandal _since its inception_. Fortunately, I have some exciting news to share: **The U.S. Supreme Court allowed states to DEFUND Planned Parenthood and instead support real, comprehensive healthcare providers.** That means states across the country can protect more women, children, and unborn babies from financially motivated abortion businesses. Folks, I won't let this thing fly under the radar any longer. Donald Trump and Mike Johnson have now flown to Pennsylvania to support this Ryan Mackenzie fella. Same district, a few months apart. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138434784/644051286/-867041604?amount=10&refcode=email_090226_actives_carville&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAxOTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTMyY2IwOWItZWJhNi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=-ytvRQPHqdpqlvfDhsqJr4IqI4alSUSBcdKMABcNe58=) Look, I've been in this business a long, long time. Folks might've killed to have my job.
I was a sideline reporter for pro football and basketball. I covered some of the most exciting games in history. I watched sports for a living. And I loved every minute, every touchdown, and every Hail Mary.
I reached the pinnacle of my career... but there was one problem:
I had to watch what I said. I was a public-facing representative for a world-class sports network. I couldn't share everything I believed, and no one really knew I was a Conservative.
So I hung up my press badge and quit my dream job so I could speak my mind.

It was the hardest decision I've ever made. I was scared, excited, and liberated - all at the same time. **
**People said I was OUT OF MY MIND. **
**But I knew God was leading me in a certain direction, and that 's no time for half-measures. I knew he had a plan for my life. So I took a leap of faith and never looked back.**
**[Now, a few years later, I’ve started a growing podcast, campaigned for commonsense in Minnesota, and now launched a campaign for U.S. Senate!](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=72f167a1e2834a11ace946e58e09697a&_e=I8ziKkqkGlV1E86uMEhbiiS445bllhXOMZs7NiZMmOnQgep0cmBWZC0rASffHR77D_iVAqsZJ6gts2oWvQuyar5dEgI-J7Z6fBKRYPKxIjwN2Lc6JZ_CWYo6BYUvQYQhkh7N7Mn7DHWfVeuew9h6cwKfNyKPTqP5GmZpd2Ua68BfdE5pFP747EWR4xdKhJTr0JX72AUdeujbeP86HzygTzylAGpuIvMCl9mOazVi4H_U628IwWFrRIChUAlfprJqHF568MBDVaV1YkPA4j5xfrqqgKJHuIwbIdGDJCM5yp-wfJ94b7PfFctXnve-f8LdApgTrXQHTJNgv2njPS5BCrIEpPCWLATRSocmWax9njtcVZbwxLkZCBMuc44fIx5DzWm-Kv3MPtoHhN-3YMeHvsZAlBLmzUqSzBfw8EW33Hud2ZRXuE5qejBUy78hP-gd57xXBLmV0V0G5CIeIwi9B8cxHv0u7AKy7YRBv-GB5fljQeaUKZhFy9lVtZfklLM44AtqE8NvfwlrWGBHsinieMM1Y8YZcJd-P6nmjGwDOGwFr7l0-pzdjaXJA0eId2Jkb_mFGSVH_9VVOmoczsC_fnRxK0H-X0ButGq-JCjeEycwJJCkpg8YWaJiNHYQvaArUc0LDSSIMVKlTrLYjVt2Gje7ewDi1rUIxVrrJWwuiNpHnQnzBLpODw25DhC2C0Pzcr5gVePE-z3gUxSHTic0E4NCXTGJ9zoHUHt99jk6gTsARtZ-LltEEyrsPjqip9P33yiiO44nkxV_g8QSgZKLdNEzxCr_jX0dr_AgmcvzNs59cHcxvPeJUqF3wr-9svT1fLFqFX2rpDlHkhfT4nJ9uw%3D%3D)**
**I believe God put me here for a reason. **
**I believe Minnesota is the land of 10,000 problems right now. **
**And I believe a no-BS, sane person who 's ALL-IN can win this seat. **
**But I 'd be lying if I said fundraising doesn't make a difference in a race like this. The far-Left is readying a FORTUNE to drown out our message and take this seat out of play. **
**Our path to victory solely depends on raising enough to keep up. **

body:
| |

Hi Peter,

Donald Trump thinks he can gut scientific research - cutting off critical work on cancer, Alzheimer’s, HIV/AIDS, wildfire prevention, pandemic preparedness and much more without anyone standing in his way.

Friend, Tennessee voters deserve a Governor who is willing to look them in the eye, answer unscripted questions, and defend their record. **_But Marsha Blackburn is refusing to debate Jerri Green._** _**Marsha hasn’t held an open town hall meeting in nearly a decade.**_ When faced with real questions from everyday Tennesseans or reporters, _Marsha turns and flees. _Her handlers know that her record— _alignment with Big Pharma, massive data centers, and corporate special interests, propped up by empty culture war distractions_ —would not survive a direct, side-by-side comparison with Jerri's platform that puts everyday Tennesseans first.

* **Lowering Everyday Costs:** Fighting back against corporate price gouging and holding utility monopolies and pharmaceutical companies accountable to bring down the cost of living.
* **Investing in Public Education: **Fully funding our public schools, raising teacher pay, and expanding access to affordable pre-K across every corner of the state.
* **Taking on Big Tech: **Advocating for a data center moratorium and more guardrails around flock cameras.
* **Safeguarding Rural Infrastructure: **Protecting local communities and natural resources from the unchecked strains of massive industrial developments like data centers without local buy-in.
* **Good-Paying Jobs:** Supporting policies that empower working people, protect the right to organize, and grow a sustainable economy from the bottom up.

## One Party Rule Stole Local Control: Builder’s Remedy Is Unconstitutional
---
Peter Ohtaki — September 1, 2026
---
State Attorney General Rob Bonta just [sent a warning to California cities](https://g3j1.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a985647a12b3b09d6e9b009&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sfchronicle.com%2Frealestate%2Farticle%2Fhousing-fight-menlo-park-bonta-22372361.php&w=6619ff0a31aa07375378c596&c=b_6a950ddbdda4493eb80beadb&l=en-US&s=evoIBuT8bttOkCSkbBY6qep_OS0%3D) that the Sacramento supermajority will back punitive **Builder’s Remedy**(SB330) projects, no matter how egregious. Bonta sent a letter ordering Menlo Park to allow **three apartment towers ranging from 17 to 39 stories** on the former Sunset Magazine campus, which will be the tallest buildings between San Francisco and San Jose. The developer N17 then sued Menlo Park to approve the project by October under AB712 or incur a minimum **$6.65 million penalty** ($10,000 for each of the project’s 665 housing units) to be paid by Menlo Park taxpayers.
#### Local Control in the Bill of Rights
The 10th Amendment of the Constitution says clearly “The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution...are reserved to the States respectively, _**or to the People.**_ ” It doesn’t mean the States exclusively, it means local control over land use decisions. We have a history of **home rule** in America. Local control goes back to [Thomas Jefferson.](https://g3j1.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a985647a12b3b09d6e9b009&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.elysian.press%2Fp%2Fthomas-jeffersons-village-states&w=6619ff0a31aa07375378c596&c=b_6a950ddbdda4493eb80beadb&l=en-US&s=763IzVgTyfK4N4lxb4htPNc1Bck%3D)
#### The Supermajority Strikes Again
The state’s **Housing Element laws** have taken away zoning and land-use decisions from city and town councils in order to meet unreasonable housing quotas. California requires all cities, towns and counties to rezone for additional housing in a **Housing Element** every 8 years under the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) - a one-size fits all **unfunded state mandate** that leaves cities with intolerable traffic and the tab for additional infrastructure like water and new classrooms, and profoundly changes the character of our communities.
#### Builder’s Remedy forces high-density over the objections and zoning of local communities
**Builder’s Remedy** (SB 330) has become the **punitive penalty** to local opposition to high-density housing. If a city doesn’t have a state-approved Housing Element rezoning plan to meet its additional housing quota, a builder can build housing that exceeds the city’s height limits. In this case, the developer N17 took advantage of an SB330 loophole by submitting the project while Menlo Park’s Housing Element was under review by the State. State Senator Christoper Cabaldon (D-Napa) said _ _ the __ Builder’s Remedy _“is intentionally supposed to be something that is so awful that cities and counties will do what we want them to do...It is serving its purpose._ ”
---
|
---
#### SB9 took away the primary role of city councils to govern land use in our communities
The state’s Housing Element also justified elimination of single family zoning in California under SB9 (Sen. Scott Weiner D-San Francisco) signed into law by Governor Newsom in 2021, despite a half-million people who’ve left California. SB9 forces increased density in residential neighborhoods, by eliminating single-family zoning to allow each lot, regardless of size, to be subdivided into 4 units. SB9 law took away our local zoning control and allows 4 housing units on your neighbor's lot, resulting in overcrowded classrooms and traffic.
#### SB9 will erode the American Dream
The goal of buying a single family house in a nice neighborhood is a big draw for immigrants like my grandparents - the American Dream. Some council members believe single family housing is exclusionary. I beg to differ. We must protect our family-friendly neighborhoods.
#### Restore Local Control

How much do you know about the Electoral College?

It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future.

You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president.

**Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. **

**That 's why I hope you'll take our National Quiz on Presidential Selection today.** It's a quick and engaging way to test your own understanding of how our presidents are elected.

**You can take your quiz by using the secure link below:**

For most of our history, the Electoral College was uncontroversial. It was understood to be a safeguard for free and representative government.

**But today, dozens of states have joined together to undermine this key constitutional protection.**

The push to "move beyond" the Constitution stems from the failure of too many schools to teach American civics properly. Many citizens today don't fully understand the importance of the Constitution and the Electoral College in preserving liberty.

To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, **reaching and teaching millions** of Americans in all 50 states.

When you take the **National Quiz on Presidential Selection** , you'll gain a clearer understanding of how the Electoral College upholds liberty--and you'll have the opportunity to **share this** information with your fellow Americans.

So please take your **National Quiz on Presidential Selection**. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

**You can take the quiz using the secure link I 've provided below: **

**As a thank-you for taking the quiz, I 'll send you a free 12-minute video with a Hillsdale College professor that explains the history and purpose of the Electoral College. **

The video provides a concise, engaging, and insightful overview of the Electoral College and its significance. It would be a great resource to send to a friend or a family member!

One other thing.

Hillsdale refuses EVERY PENNY of government funding--even indirectly through student loans or grants--so that we can pursue truth and defend liberty independent of meddling bureaucrats in Washington, D.C. That's why your support matters so much.

So, after you take your quiz, please also consider giving a **tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, or even $100** to help us share this video with millions of Americans--especially young people who don't understand how the Constitution preserves liberty through the Electoral College. Your gift also funds our other nationwide educational outreach.

Thank you for standing with Hillsdale College in the effort to educate Americans about the Constitution and safeguard the principles of liberty. Good luck on the quiz and enjoy your video!

To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, reaching and teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states. Hillsdale refuses EVERY PENNY of government funding--even indirectly through student loans or grants--so that we can pursue truth and defend liberty independent of meddling bureaucrats in Washington, D.C. So, after you take your quiz, please also consider giving a tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, or even $100 to help us share this video with millions of Americans--especially young people who don't understand how the Constitution preserves liberty through the Electoral College. Your gift also funds our other nationwide educational outreach. Thank you for standing with Hillsdale College in the effort to educate Americans about the Constitution and safeguard the principles of liberty. Good luck on the quiz and enjoy your video! Warm regards, Bill Gray '01 Vice President Institutional Advancement Hillsdale College P.S. name: Ken Martin (via DNC HQ)
subject: My question for you
body:
---
Derek, Ken Martin here. I’ve spent my career organizing on the ground and talking to voters every day. I learned from experience that winning strategies are the ones guided by regular people, not pundits. Even as DNC Chair, it’s incredibly important to me to hear from people who are doing the work — making calls, knocking on doors, and registering voters. That’s why I’ve had my team gather our most dedicated grassroots supporters from Pennsylvania. Derek, you’re one of those Pennsylvania Democrats. Winning control of the House and Senate depends on knowing which issues matter most to this team, so I hope you’ll take a minute to [**join my focus group and answer a few questions to help guide our midterm strategy**](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260902-ken-focus-group/?refcode=em_20260902_8919_fr&akid=8919%2E22930333%2E9JWdX_) **[JOIN THE CHAIR’S FOCUS GROUP](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260902-ken-focus-group/?refcode=em_20260902_8919_fr&akid=8919%2E22930333%2E9JWdX_)** Trump’s chaos, his tariffs, and his war of choice with Iran have been wreaking havoc on American families. I want you to know that my team and I think every day about what the cost of this presidency has been to the American people. **Our best shot at stopping him is by electing Democratic majorities who will put a real check on his power.** [**So please, take a minute to fill out this survey and help us cross the finish line to victory this November.**](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260902-ken-focus-group/?refcode=em_20260902_8919_fr&akid=8919%2E22930333%2E9JWdX_) **Your input is invaluable to this team.** Thank you, Ken Martin
DNC Chair

# [Trump opened Venezuela, Chevron just bet $7B that Venezuela oil is back](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chevron **[will invest more than $7 billion over 5 years in Venezuela](https://substack.com/redirect/efbb3064-0c05-4c2e-a6b3-5e92e88acbea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and aims to more than double joint-venture output to about 600,000 barrels a day, the largest concrete U.S. corporate bet yet beside Trump's NABEP deal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New acreage, better terms:** Updated fiscal and legal terms add Orinoco Belt acreage at Petroindependencia and Petropiar, where Chevron holds 49% and 30% stakes after an April working-interest increase.
* **Costs stay under $20:** Yahoo Finance reported total **[costs are expected to remain below $20 a barrel](https://substack.com/redirect/d212ed3e-21cd-41e0-9264-b56d0031f14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d212ed3e-21cd-41e0-9264-b56d0031f14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)after output across the three joint ventures[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5c317073-a9b0-429c-aa95-56661bf92cd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[already rose 15%](https://substack.com/redirect/5c317073-a9b0-429c-aa95-56661bf92cd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5c317073-a9b0-429c-aa95-56661bf92cd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)this year.
* **More firms sign Wednesday:** The Wall Street Journal said other oil-and-gas companies are **[expected to sign Caracas production deals later Wednesday.](https://substack.com/redirect/37aced68-0ef4-405d-b6ef-0ed076177e2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **$100B NABEP hole remains:** North American Blue Energy Partners must raise about $100 billion for fields holding some 65 billion barrels; a U.S. official said Washington is putting up "zero" taxpayer dollars.

# [Iran tried to shut Hormuz, 17 million barrels still sailed](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Energy Secretary Chris Wright **[told CNBC more than 17 million barrels](https://substack.com/redirect/67986b1a-3faf-4104-83aa-033855ef913d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** moved through Hormuz on Monday, a wartime record on the U.S.-escorted Oman corridor, even as Iran claimed two tankers hit mines.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Wright says the card is slipping:** Wright said Tehran is "losing that card" and that oil and gas will flow from the Gulf "with or without Iran," speaking from Venezuela.
* **CENTCOM hits air defenses:** U.S. forces struck Iranian air-defense, communications, and radar sites after attempted attacks on shipping and American service members; Jordan intercepted 10 of 13 missiles.
* **Diesel reprints wartime heat:** AAA put the U.S. retail diesel average at $5.688 a gallon, the highest since April's wartime peak, as Brent hovered near $94 after briefly tagging $97.
* **Bessent goes after the cash:** Bessent said the U.S. will freeze IRGC trust accounts in the British Virgin Islands and $100 million properties, and cut dollar access for entities still doing business with the regime.

# [Trump's Treasury chief just boxed China in at the G20](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d9352cc3-a80f-4d62-b180-55943637f391?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[China was the sole G20 holdout against a statement condemning"cheap exports"](https://substack.com/redirect/d9352cc3-a80f-4d62-b180-55943637f391?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and non-market overcapacity, and also objected to language on Hormuz disruptions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Chairman statement stands anyway:** Bessent said China, holder of the world's largest current-account surplus, dissented from his chairman's statement on overcapacity, IMF surveillance, and G20 external debt.
* **Gulf oil is China 's problem too:** Bessent said China gets 50% of its energy from the Gulf, agrees Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, and that it is "incumbent upon China" to help reopen Hormuz.
* **Xi keeps Pezeshkian off camera:** Xi met Iran's president for several minutes at the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, but Chinese state media omitted the encounter weeks before a planned Trump-Xi meeting.
* **Optics without a blank check:** Analysts said Beijing is keeping a private channel open while signaling dissatisfaction and refusing to look like it is siding with Tehran.

# [AI tokens just hit 97 cents, OpenAI's pricing power cracked](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Silicon Data's **[LLM Token Expenditure Index fell to 97 cents on Monday,](https://substack.com/redirect/caba9eb1-aa46-48a5-97da-983d7cbfe562?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** its lowest reading since launch late last year and more than 50% below the summer high, as cheaper Chinese models and lab price cuts landed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Open-weight models set the floor:** The drop was driven by lower-priced open-source Chinese models such as Moonshot's Kimi K3 and by late-July OpenAI cuts on two GPT-5.6 models.
* **Labs eat the deflation:** Syz Group's Charles-Henry Monchau said foundation-model labs are most exposed because token deflation hits revenue while compute commitments stay fixed.
* **Moat moves to distribution:** Monchau said the edge must shift from raw model capability, "where the open-weight gap is now measured in months," toward distribution, memory, and context.
* **Most tasks still get done:** Silicon Data research head Steve Hou said today's cheaper tokens "provide sufficient capabilities for most tasks," even as Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT compete on price.

# [Tampa now has Waymo and Tesla robotaxis. The war is on](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Waymo is starting **[paid driverless rides in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa,](https://substack.com/redirect/26496317-750a-4b44-95f1-44142af09ba7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** taking its fleet past 4,000 vehicles in 14 U.S. cities as Amazon-owned Zoox begins supervised testing in Houston and San Diego.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Half a million rides a week:** Waymo already runs more than 500,000 U.S. robotaxi rides a week and aims to cross 1 million by the end of 2026, with dozens of cars in each new city growing to hundreds.
* **Ojai vans bring Gemini:** Newer Ojai vehicles, built on a Zeekr minivan chassis in Arizona, add sliding doors, three cabin screens, sixth-generation driverless tech, and a Gemini entertainment system.
* **Zoox still trails paid scale:** Zoox's only paid service is Las Vegas; Houston and San Diego start this month with human supervisors, taking Zoox to 12 U.S. markets.
* **Tesla talks Thursday:** Tesla plans to share more on its driverless Cybercab and Robotaxi service Thursday, while Goldman sees the U.S. robotaxi market rising from about $3 billion in 2026 to $19 billion in 2030.

# [Trump's DOJ just put Walmart and Costco in the beef-price fight](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Justice Department **[expanded its beef-price antitrust investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/d40c183e-4cd8-4066-9465-fb71e51c98ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from the Big Four packers to 8 major grocers, including Kroger, Walmart, Costco, Amazon, Publix, Albertsons, Aldi, and Ahold Delhaize.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Packers still sit at 85%:** The May probe of JBS, Cargill, Tyson Foods, and National Beef remains open; those four control more than 85% of U.S. beef processing.
* **Three million documents already:** DOJ said it is reviewing more than 3 million documents and called beef prices "a critical concern to Americans, and a priority for this Justice Department."
* **Whistleblowers can take a cut:** Attorney General Todd Blanche said tipsters who help secure a criminal penalty above $1 million can recover 15% to 30% of the money DOJ collects.
* **Herd is at a 1950s low:** The U.S. had about 86.2 million head of cattle and calves as of Jan. 1, the lowest since the 1950s, as officials also weigh tariff-free imports of up to 300,000 metric tons.

# [Uber just cut 3,300 jobs to race Tesla and Waymo](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Uber **[will cut 10% of its workforce,](https://substack.com/redirect/92b5f0b2-fe08-4efd-800c-f2f13fc0f67a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** about 3,300 jobs on a year-end 2025 headcount of around 34,000, as CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said the company must get "simpler and faster."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d6d71f-fe67-46b7-8762-813c3beab4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tiny teams get halved:** Uber is cutting small one-to-two-report teams by nearly half and trimming employees seven steps from the CEO by 20%.
* **Hubs win, remote shrinks:** More staff will concentrate in New York and San Francisco hubs, with only about 1% still allowed to work remotely.
* **Not framed as an AI purge:** The company did not blame the cuts on artificial intelligence; Khosrowshahi said a leaner Uber means clearer ownership and more time building than coordinating.
* **Shares bid the news:** Uber stock rose nearly 2% in morning trading after the announcement.

Dear Patriot,

I stood on a porch in Detroit last week and showed a woman a photograph of her own absentee ballot return envelope from the 2020 election. She looked at the signature and said, "That's me right there."

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODd9AAwAAAAAAretdF81KKKaci6c8N9UkqCQlKo2xQK6ED5XIerXeqoySq_Jd5S8vl-XlE0d280neBO5APp53oKlfEKHm4sOZKZaLjagWehU7AWsZQXL7Q
Then I showed her a second envelope , issued to the same voter, at the same address, for the same election.

She looked at it for a moment and said: "That's not me. I don't know who that person is."

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODd9AAwAAAAAAretdF82wgIvnZogECj6uvUo3JBk1Q57XSS4HlBfV4zgNpc3XL5yNNqY739w9GCnWqFt95or5LFLGpemnL7S-_GUKTcHoiKNVwsFjdTajw

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODd9AAwAAAAAAretdF83Tj6tNSOUvvOsApY-i_vrUZHdYrpj8qJdX0Co1qYddS3ZrATDzSSn4PrSIDHEZlefGF-MM3EKfPD1Wdm6v0e56eyeW-1YcA6ufg

Here is the part I cannot get out of my head. She told us the City of Detroit had already contacted her about that ballot back in 2020, specifically because the signature did not match the one they had on file for her. The city already knew about the discrepancy, and that envelope was still received, still stamped, and never rejected.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODd9AAwAAAAAAretdF84o-s7_Z3qrSlaGYyi5wvC2GQrx0A7WkwajfWGSnn9QMiOF87ox5hWZENONofvic4nVjUBE7hv7VkhK0YFgF0lHJUKNZsZ6bHF_A
Help me find out who signed it.

We did not obtain that document from a leak, a whistleblower, or a lucky break, but the slow way instead, and the slow way is exactly the reason almost nobody in America does this particular kind of work.

It took our team three to four years of Freedom of Information Act requests to pry these certified records out of the City of Detroit Law Department. That produced millions of pages, which my investigators went through by hand, the analog way, one envelope at a time, because the system is layered and complicated enough that hardly anyone ever reaches the end of it.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODd9AAwAAAAAAretdF85lM7YcQ7hpUTz0xX1rjwSb_tl2YEgBSkL5QormfLqwskEJ2fpfgCEA4kFUBLBcMQE87rv9zHVGRDOEo6OyqAH_XxEt1AKGia-Ww
FUND THE INVESTIGATION — CHIP IN $35 NOW
Here is what turned up: duplicate absentee ballot return envelopes issued to the same registered voters. We scanned the barcodes on those envelopes and found that the voter identification numbers matched perfectly, while the ballot numbers did not. On several of them, the two signatures look nothing alike, with one envelope signed in careful cursive and the other in an illegible scrawl.

So we did the thing that almost nobody in journalism bothers to do anymore, which is that we went and knocked on the doors.

One of those addresses turned out to be a burned out, abandoned building on Greenfield Road, where the local police confirmed that nobody has lived for years and the flooring was not safe enough to stand on. Somebody is still registered to vote at that address, and the records show that person cast a ballot in 2020 and again in 2024.

At another door, a man looked down at two envelopes with his own name signed on both of them and said, "That's illegal, man." Then he asked me if we could scrape one of them off.

A woman threatened to put her dog on me, and another man ordered us off his property, so we left. When our security guard could not determine whether a pit bull in the next yard was actually chained up, he walked toward the animal to find out, so that nobody else had to.

That is the job, and that is precisely what your money pays for.

Friends,There is a pretty stark difference between the way Mike Kelly runs his campaign and the way I run mine.According to his campaign finance filings, Mike is spending **$12,500 every month** with Fresh Ink Freelance, the consulting firm owned by Cole and Danielle Robinson. On top of that, Mike is spending another **$6,250 per month** for campaign management and finance.That’s **$18,750 every month** before buying a single mailer, digital ad or yard sign.Compare that to my campaign.I paid my consultant **$1,500 per month** in April, May and June of 2025. Then I took three months off from consulting altogether because I wanted to conserve campaign funds. I resumed at $1,500 per month in October and stayed at that level through June 2026.Only in July, as we entered the heart of the election, did I increase that investment to **$2,500 per month.** My campaign manager? **Volunteer.** My finance director? **Volunteer.** Now, campaign dollars aren't taxpayer dollars. I understand the difference. But spending habits tell you something. When I have limited resources, my instinct is to prioritize, find efficiencies, rely on people who believe in the mission and make every dollar work harder.**Mike's instinct is to spend. Mine is to find a better way.** And when we're talking about who should oversee a **$1.9 billion county budget** , I think that distinction matters.If you have contributed to my campaign, I hope this gives you something else: **confidence in how I am using the money you entrusted to me.** Those are your hard-earned dollars, and I take that responsibility seriously. I am not interested in spending money just because it is there. I want every dollar to have a purpose and produce a result.Money matters in a campaign, absolutely. But I do not need millions of dollars to compete effectively. **I know how to prioritize, stretch resources, build a strong team and get results without wasting money.** Now that you know how carefully I am spending the dollars entrusted to this campaign, will you chip in to help us get this message out?Johnson County does not have to accept the status quo. We do not have to accept a spending-first mentality that says the answer is always more money. We can demand better. We can prioritize. We can spend smarter. And we can elect a Chair who knows the difference.If you believe that too, I’d be grateful for your help getting that message in front of more voters.[**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/UXvDBYAtTpW?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) Thank you for your support!Fighting for you,Karen CrnkovichCandidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

| | | | Peter, Will you help me put God back in your town schools? Specifically, I'm asking you to sign the "[**Schools Need a Bible Revival**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=20a2b529058a4bf9bd1acfa95b1c9c94&_e=hQHL7XDgJT_Pqe54l5Q1SS-oXp9UqxOSuw_qLps3-dvxOxICTdL_vrfB0E0F8SbG4bNq1RbqX8XyeFyPxfx0unK36rEUlw2e-38rO6-aywOW7PLvlJuiqY80aM-E4DRS9JgqcXH6k5_GNugCQsNkMRxfXCT28SRy2kYnw8OQv9d7JEPkL19D_GgSOKp5IJLKwP-8Q2VaRP5MoHctFmLOC3JGbO1fP0MOyiEJeydW0W_rzE7Z_OT3ypKqxpAdAOf2F68c8TeqUv2dorWPZw6qpgDzv0Gm0BhEYN2UAc3Pis1cm8YGbzktsbbWnKysl26MtdYRkXFM_wmnG5RhYDN96gsmUm3V1v6Wg0TPphcjMjDnngEO00hHeqAKRKnLpzCWEHup6sKOnsz8kLN3G9q8kanK0xwGLhpmXsIg71O2_gOxYbw5NwgyY7gh3ckzIpE_PsIJaMefXF7Tw4UuTu44xdmzWov_KdMm7n-_7mYeCQRqTvSr9uQykv2JpBBwqK-IZKMDxuBoKgyt-DWMtCUd4XNuRQRSuZKXne0F3CyHOlbpsl2P7jQDrxXtWgDULwmgbzgPzYWIaJY8pU6SIfRtfYcct8QSKeouXLo6nhil-FCPCzclUcRhzDd8cBUvKNL6Pl7Sm2_sHuFsBzyZHVFQXt7DrYOSj17bIQZzA1sHzV6SiciPDTAMAG_3itlP9zOzb_qoV0yJy0nS3D0iPghahhzzEqM8Yts4r2h3ImT-xEI%3D)" petition and tell your Governor that the children in your community deserve to hear that: They are wonderfully made in the very image of God. And that God is calling them to love Him above all else. What a country we'd be, if all of America's children had just a little bit of God's Word in their lives - like you did. But in 1963, in a wrongly decided Supreme Court case, the Left ripped the everyday reading of the Bible out of public schools. **And the results speak for themselves: more violence, divorce, abortion, clean_body: What Happened When the Bible Left Schools? Now we're going to get biblical values back into public schools. | | | | Peter, Will you help me put God back in your town schools? Specifically, I'm asking you to sign the "" petition and tell your Governor that the children in your community deserve to hear that: They are wonderfully made in the very image of God. And that God is calling them to love Him above all else. What a country we'd be, if all of America's children had just a little bit of God's Word in their lives - like you did. But in 1963, in a wrongly decided Supreme Court case, the Left ripped the everyday reading of the Bible out of public schools. And the results speak for themselves: more violence, divorce, abortion, drug addiction, depression, and the breakdown of the family. It is only fitting that during the 250th Anniversary of our independence, we put Biblical lessons BACK into our public schools. Your signature on your "" petition tells our representatives that you want biblical lessons put back in schools. Your signed " " petition is going straight to my friends at BRAVE FOR GOOD. BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group behind my "See You at the Library" movement featured on Fox News, that gets conservative Story Hours into public libraries to counter the Left's "Drag Queen Story Hours." BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group that got an historic conservative Story Hour into the Library of Congress last year! And BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group that will get the Biblical values you cherish - and that America was founded upon - back into public schools this year! HOW? We've designed a mini-curriculum for America's 250th Anniversary that teaches children about the role of the Bible in our nation's Founding and emphasizes the Founding values that have made our country great. Last year I got into three public schools to reach 1,400 children with biblical lessons. That's why BRAVE FOR GOOD is getting ready for the battle by collecting stacks of petitions. Your signed " " petition tells our representatives that the Supreme Court ruling that took the Bible out of schools only specified that the Bible could not be mandatory reading. The 1963 ruling 100% allows for the Bible to be taught in a historical or cultural context! And why wouldn’t it be? In every corner of the world, the Bible is considered one of the greatest books ever written. Of course children should learn about it in your taxpayer-funded schools! But radical educators will try to keep anything to do with the Bible out of our schools and when they do, BRAVE FOR GOOD will be ready to counter them with thousands of signed petitions. Every petition you send digitally must still be delivered, verified, securely collected, and tabulated before it can be presented - and That means your gift today puts hundreds of new voices on the record before the deadline. Together with BRAVE FOR GOOD and patriots like you, we got conservative and patriotic values back into public libraries. Now we're going to get biblical values back into public schools. Only God can lead our nation back to His Word. But you and I are called to do our part too. Thank you for standing with us. May God bless you, | | | Kirk Cameron BRAVE For Good | | | | | | | | | P.S. Team Mackenzie,
Labor Day weekend is here — and that means it’s time to push harder than ever!
To kick off the weekend, Team Mackenzie is taking on a BIG goal: 1,000 doors in ONE DAY on Saturday, September 5th!
This is the moment for us to hit the streets, talk with voters, build momentum, and help deliver a Republican victory up and down the ballot.
We’re asking every volunteer to step up and help us reach this goal. 20 doors, 40 doors, or even 50 doors — every door matters!
🏆 BONUS: The top 3 volunteers who knock the most doors will receive a gift card as a thank-you for going above and beyond!
You can get connected with our team ahead of time or join one of our door launches on Saturday. We’ll provide everything you need — including your door list through our app and campaign materials.

Mackenzie HQ — Coffee and Doughnuts Provided
1125 S. Cedar Crest Blvd. Suite 106
Allentown, PA
10:00 AM
Northampton County Republican Committee — Pizza and Hoagies Provided
2523 Willow Park Rd.
Bethlehem, PA 18020
12:00 PM
Whether you can knock 20 doors or 50, we need you out there!
If you can’t make either launch but would like to knock doors on your own, we can get you the materials and your door list ahead of Saturday.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | One student learned and tried it on a little-known stock.
