Vincent has been serving the public for many years as a Sheriff Deputy and city council member as an advocate for the people. Vincent has run for office and has lots of real world political experience getting things done as well as voicing his opposition to much of the political voices in the Washington State legislature. Vincent has lots to say about the business climate of Washington State and how he belives the Blue Dog Dems have made it an unfriendly place to do business. In a nation that strives to stand as a beacon of democratic values, it's shameful to need to write these words: Our President is once again attempting to undermine the voting rights of Americans.
And now the Supreme Court just paved the way for Donald Trump's attacks on the right to vote by mail to move forward.
Donald Trump, who voted by mail himself, wants to make it harder for Americans to cast their ballots by mail.
Trump and his Republican cronies know that they're unpopular, so they're going to extreme lengths to sow chaos and confusion ahead of the midterms.
The Constitution gives states the power to run elections, but Donald Trump has spent much of his second term trying to upend American voting habits.
* He has tried to push through the **SAVE America Act** , a hyper-partisan bill that would disenfranchise millions of eligible voters by changing requirements.
* He has tried to **require proof of citizenship** , demanding states hand over sensitive data or that Americans bring passports or other complex paperwork with them to register to vote. Again and again, studies show voting by non-citizens is extremely rare, and these barriers would only serve to disenfranchise eligible voters.
* He has tried to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterms, threatening to **throw state systems into chaos and confuse millions of voters** at the moment when clarity and consistency matter most.

**Republicans are afraid they will lose their House and Senate majorities, so they are trying to stop certain Americans from voting altogether. We can 't let them.**
**[My team is working on gathering 20,000 signatures to send a clear message that Americans won't put up with continued assaults on democracy.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/354b17cd-8ef3-4871-a1ce-ceb5c7347e2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **

* * *
##### `A personal note from Sen. Jacky Rosen:`
##### `My work in the Senate has always been defined by who I am and where I come from. Growing up as the granddaughter of immigrants and the daughter of a World War II veteran, my family instilled in me the values of hard work, determination, and persistence at a young age.`
##### `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.`
##### `Senate Democrats like me are the only thing standing in the way of Trump's extreme agenda that will hurt everyday Americans. That's why I need people like you on my side to help defend our progress and reclaim power from the GOP.`
##### `If you're with me, will you chip in now to help Democrats take back the Senate majority?`

We can see this fight coming from a mile away, Peter. And it’s a fight we can win. Indiana map manipulators are potentially gearing up for another attempt at gerrymandering their congressional map, and here’s why: **“Trump redistricting advocate set to become new Indiana Senate leader”**
— _The Times of Northwest Indiana_ Last year, several Republicans in the Indiana Senate — including the Republican Senate Leader — resisted extreme pressure from the White House and rejected a new gerrymander. Since then, Trump has sought revenge against the Republicans who didn't toe the line. Many have lost their seats, and now the next Senate Leader — who “nearly single-handedly controls the fate of proposed new laws” — will be a Trump yes-man on redistricting. But we saw how lawmakers responded to their constituents last time around, when Hoosiers made their voices heard against gerrymandering. That public pressure convinced a bipartisan majority to shut down an outrageous attempt at mid-decade map manipulation. **The fair maps movement won this fight before, and we can do it again — the other side has made strides forward, and we can’t afford to wait to start fighting back. The surveillance video showing Lyons Township Clerk Elyse Hoffenberg and Bridgeview Mayor Steven Landek kissing inside her government office after hours has now become the most-watched video in Illinois Review history.

The story has since been picked up by the New York Post, Daily Mail, Hindustan Times, The Times of India and Barstool Sports, giving the controversy national and international exposure.

Friend 🐾,

I’m barking in your inbox today because I’ve been one busy pup! My mom brought me along to a very special place: **Chaco Canyon!**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16410?refcode=jtk1307-fr-nd&t=2&akid=12168%2E400544%2EyTCtgg)
I got to explore, take in all the new smells, and spend some time outside with my mom. But I know Chaco isn’t just a great place for a walk. It’s a sacred place that means so much to my mom, Tribal communities, and generations of New Mexicans.
**Chaco holds a special place in my mom’s heart. She’s spent years fighting to protect it and the other sacred lands that make New Mexico so special. _**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### Dr. Eric Lullove spends his days trying to close wounds on the legs and feet of people who worked outdoors for a living. When EPA approved a new weedkiller for American food crops this July, he did the thing almost nobody does. He pulled the agency's own registration file and read the whole thing.
##### What he found is below.
##### I'm not going to pretend this one is fun. It's the kind of story that exists only because a physician sat down with a federal docket on his own time. The trade press didn't do it. The agencies didn't do it. And the Health Secretary who built a national movement on the chemicals in our food said nothing at all.
##### That is what your subscription pays for. Not takes. Documents.
##### The first half of this piece is free, and I want you to send it to everyone you know who eats. The rest--the children's safety margin EPA erased, the enzyme this chemical shuts down that your own blood needs, and the one paragraph where the agency explains why it will not add the risks together--is for paid subscribers.

* * *
_**By Dr. Eric J. Lullove**_
On July 1, 2026, the Environmental Protection Agency approved a chemical called trifludimoxazin for use on American food crops. Corn. Soybeans. Wheat. Oats. Peanuts. Oranges. Apples. Pears. Almonds, pecans, pistachios, and walnuts. Beans and peas.
You have almost certainly never heard of it. Neither had I, until I read the file.
I have spent my career treating wounds that will not heal--mostly on the legs and feet of people who worked outdoors for a living. So I went and pulled EPA's own registration record, docket number EPA-HQ-OPP-2022-0649, and read it start to finish.
I want to be careful here. I am not going to tell you this chemical will give you cancer. I am going to tell you something worse: nobody knows, because nobody looked--and the agency wrote down that it wasn't going to look.
## The Names
Institutions don't sign documents. People do.
**Ed Messina** , Director of the Office of Pesticide Programs, signed the registration decision. His name is on the front page.
**Douglas Troutman** runs the office above him--Assistant Administrator for Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention. He spent 18 years at the American Cleaning Institute, a chemical industry trade group, before the Senate confirmed him in December 2025. When EPA announced his confirmation, the pitch was that he "understands the companies that make them." That was the selling point.
**Lee Zeldin** , the EPA Administrator, runs the agency. When the Make America Healthy Again report first raised alarms about farm chemicals, Zeldin went on a press call and assured everyone it would not lead to tougher rules. It didn't.
**Robert F. Kennedy Jr.** didn't sign anything. That is exactly the problem.
Kennedy built a national movement on the claim that the chemicals in our food are making Americans sick. He runs Health and Human Services. He sits on the MAHA Commission. The FDA reports to him, and FDA is the agency that actually checks food for pesticide residue. He had every lever.
In February 2026, when the President invoked the Defense Production Act to boost domestic glyphosate production, Kennedy--who once promised to ban the stuff--said "we must safeguard America's national security first." Four months later EPA approved its fifth PFAS-family pesticide of this administration. Kennedy said nothing. No statement. No referral. No request for further study.
He also has no confirmed FDA commissioner. Marty Makary resigned in May. A food-industry attorney, Kyle Diamantas, has been running the agency on an acting basis ever since. Heidi Overton, a White House aide, was nominated in August. That is the leadership standing between this chemical and your kitchen.

The Names Institutions don't sign documents. People do. Ed Messina , Director of the Office of Pesticide Programs, signed the registration decision. His name is on the front page. Douglas Troutman runs the office above him--Assistant Administrator for Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention. He spent 18 years at the American Cleaning Institute, a chemical industry trade group, before the Senate confirmed him in December 2025. When EPA announced his confirmation, the pitch was that he "understands the companies that make them." That was the selling point. Lee Zeldin , the EPA Administrator, runs the agency. When the Make America Healthy Again report first raised alarms about farm chemicals, Zeldin went on a press call and assured everyone it would not lead to tougher rules. It didn't. Robert F. Kennedy Jr.** didn't sign anything. That is exactly the problem. Kennedy built a national movement on the claim that the chemicals in our food are making Americans sick. He runs Health and Human Services. He sits on the MAHA Commission. The FDA reports to him, and FDA is the agency that actually checks food for pesticide residue. He had every lever. In February 2026, when the President invoked the Defense Production Act to boost domestic glyphosate production, Kennedy--who once promised to ban the stuff--said "we must safeguard America's national security first." Four months later EPA approved its fifth PFAS-family pesticide of this administration. Kennedy said nothing. No statement. No referral. No request for further study. He also has no confirmed FDA commissioner. Marty Makary resigned in May. A food-industry attorney, Kyle Diamantas, has been running the agency on an acting basis ever since. Heidi Overton, a White House aide, was nominated in August. That is the leadership standing between this chemical and your kitchen. **Here are just 5 things I’ll be fighting for in Congress: **
1. **Making healthcare more affordable and accessible.** My opponent, Bill Huizenga, voted to rip healthcare from hundreds of thousands of Michigan families, all so he could give himself — and his billionaire buddies — huge tax breaks.
2. **Cracking down on corporations who drive up costs.** Everyday families are drowning under the rising costs of everything from healthcare premiums to housing to groceries — and the folks in Washington aren’t helping.
3. **Banning members of Congress from trading stocks.** Members of Congress have access to insider information and shouldn’t be using their position of power to enrich themselves while in office.
4. **Getting special interest money out of politics, like big oil and utilities.** While utility costs skyrocket, Huizenga voted to gut programs that help hardworking Michigan families cover their hefty electricity bills — bills from the companies that fill Huizenga’s campaign war chest.
5. **Opposing endless wars that are making life more expensive.** Michigan families are paying the price for Trump’s reckless war in Iran while he gets richer off his oil and gas stocks. We need to hold him accountable and bring prices down.

Team Tran is mobilizing ahead as we get closer to Election Day! During this busy month, I met with many of you across our district, hearing the issues that matter most — from protecting affordable healthcare to lowering everyday costs.
One of these issues that resonates deeply with our community is uplifting our vibrant small businesses — the family-run, brick-and-mortar restaurants, shops, pharmacies, and markets.
As a member of the House Small Business Committee, I’ve prioritized visiting small businesses across our district to hear directly from local business owners on how Congress can better support them. I hope you take some time to read more about these visits below.

| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%._ _It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._

Any day now, students are arriving on campus and the Abortion Lobby's lackeys are waiting to ambush them with lies.

**That 's why nearly 90% of Planned Parenthoods are located within walking distance of a college campus!**

To expose the true impact of the Abortion Goliath, many of our college groups will place 1,190 bright pink crosses right smack in the middle of campus as a _Cemetery of the Innocents_ display to serve as a stark reminder of the reality that abortion kills preborn babies.

Pro-Life Friend, I've always thought of _Students for Life_ as your organization. That's why I want you to be part of our witness.

[So would you please agree to sponsor a cross today with a tax-deductible gift of $10](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=c4be262700974edfaeb3d6334fb7f6c0&_e=-xURkEpxVIVZ8muAg1dmZfySpkUgLbNkPNP78YoZUKgAksepk7RRzwimYHAIUGfMv9Uo3baxXJ4o4Cwvkwr7LOiPh2ffcTXhtrz0wE2hAGb5FvBRBmoLwWEYGxpaBEM4WDYdpBvc77qgR1qftF25fbGSRbOk14p_SPolh4Q990cqJJao7zIjOuQy2c3OvKkFeOMKtD0yelJ49VG8uMYRmbnmo6plq7fjiYLg8nL851puFjBk1xR3hBzUFIFX_r_U86qs39pRzTjlmKmzZ36XFsisExdbDudQ_u6FIiTVIB-7lJmCWUBF8QMwi19_GWZ1E_3Q3rFVpZ4yk4Vu3nWki9ZnxiFBuv0_R3iVmXhq4w5KDSmjtyUScDQ4Kx6iM83ie5VubkbSZvs8Z041PZj5MaRemnfUfeLToFGsstG305ItjpGJomyS3nvSV83Ou6334icMdtedpl0H1iANRuxeeeNZMOOoZMJsk0D08_QqYEYmFSmBPXA9HvdHpqXv8S98ZqP-adhtAcnfwwFcXSrbODJRpOuDI5rOv-eW_cAYakjdOKYs-yMPFc8xoIj53dY_xlxfmsIvdaztrcv8jHioblpYGqoghn8ewIEfs7DNytrWhLVPZDg1tlY12KuSwhc9)**?**

Your sponsorship will provide a voice for the voiceless right where it needs to be heard most - on American college campuses.

Planned Parenthood sets traps for young college girls as they walk on campus - traps that end in pain, regret ... and the bloodshed of hundreds of thousands of preborn babies every year.

Our campaign just crossed $2 million raised for this race — powered by thousands of everyday Floridians and small-dollar donors. That milestone belongs to people like you, and I’m deeply grateful to everyone who has contributed along the way. But this fight is far from finished. James Uthmeier is taking millions from special interests and using his office to do their dirty work. Last week alone, the Republican Attorneys General Association announced it is pumping six figures into his campaign as part of a national fund backing Republican AGs in states across the country. Peter, we're just over two months from Election Day, and this is the stretch where we can't afford to let up. Peter,
Tucker here, Chaz's campaign manager.
Charlie Hatcher has spent this entire campaign saying he's the farmers' candidate.
He's aligned himself with the administration at every turn. But when the administration announced a plan to flood the market with Argentinian beef, putting Tennessee cattle ranchers at real risk, Hatcher didn't stand up. He asked a few polite questions and called it a day.
That's not standing up for farmers. That's covering your bases.
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/8ELnGNjD6XAroL3tvRlNQA~~/AAUS1hA~/Og-p-U0_Ira2ryqhzj-ISTONsAiHT4Nf2UjwdHqgilizQjMqyWqHAG18sy1_sqbjUH-dEL_U4LzzcoTSzcx2GDIH4GsB3Dcw2vocZZ_skgTBLe8DZHpcCRmWlaC_lXtVDc1i-V-LmKmlCUz_VZfcARpqiG_0sToH7P0gzxI9bdCw-VMw8jfaYpFl4hvMMbqdBxuWvj4rBDWRCxF8RBj5_ywhZwUSDdRSwpXBWy8JLY_0YcINxTMeYVbZ0IHwpaDy7t8Nz3hwK-aN3NW8WmRpYA~~)
Chaz doesn't operate that way. The Tennessee Farm Bureau, headquartered right in his hometown of Columbia, has spoken out clearly on this issue. Chaz stands with them, without hedging, without waiting to see which way the wind blows.
As mayor of Columbia and a former Farm Bureau intern, Chaz knows what it means when the Farm Bureau raises its voice. It means something is wrong, and someone needs to fight back. That's the kind of congressman TN-05 deserves.

When I got off active duty and came back home to the great state of Georgia, I quickly realized that despite having thousands of service members in our communities, **_Georgia is not a veteran-friendly state,_** between state taxes on military retirement and a healthcare system that treats veterans like an afterthought.

My last assignment was in Israel. I went from leading troops in high-stakes environments to coming back home and experiencing the sudden crash that so many service members face when transitioning back to civilian life. I knew I needed help, so I called Fort Benning. They directed me to a local mental health facility. I pulled up to that clinic as General Shawn Harris. I walked to the counter, and the receptionist looked right at me and said: _"We don't take TRICARE anymore."_ I had served 40 years. I had the rank, and I had the phone numbers to call people high up in the chain of command to fix my situation. But what if I was an E-4? If a young Specialist walked into that clinic without a star on their shoulder or a direct line to a general, they would have been turned away with nowhere to go. Without help, they could have ended up dead. I walked back out, sat in my car, and thought: **_This is why I 'm getting into politics._** **My blood boils when politicians like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth treat our military like a political backdrop or talk about veterans' benefits as something to slash and privatize.** Pete Hegseth and the political class in Washington love to wrap themselves in the flag, but when our service members come home broken, struggling, or needing care, they look the other way. They treat the men and women who put their lives on the line like line items on a spreadsheet instead of human beings who earned their care. Our troops and veterans don't need political posturing or lectures on culture wars from political appointees--they need a healthcare system that actually answers the phone when they call for help. I fought for this country for four decades, and I'm not going to sit quietly while politicians neglect the men and women who served alongside me. clean_body: | | When I got off active duty and came back home to the great state of Georgia, I quickly realized that despite having thousands of service members in our communities, Georgia is not a veteran-friendly state, between state taxes on military retirement and a healthcare system that treats veterans like an afterthought. | My last assignment was in Israel. I went from leading troops in high-stakes environments to coming back home and experiencing the sudden crash that so many service members face when transitioning back to civilian life. I knew I needed help, so I called Fort Benning. They directed me to a local mental health facility. I pulled up to that clinic as General Shawn Harris. I walked to the counter, and the receptionist looked right at me and said: "We don't take TRICARE anymore." I had served 40 years. I had the rank, and I had the phone numbers to call people high up in the chain of command to fix my situation. But what if I was an E-4? If a young Specialist walked into that clinic without a star on their shoulder or a direct line to a general, they would have been turned away with nowhere to go. Without help, they could have ended up dead. I walked back out, sat in my car, and thought: This is why I 'm getting into politics. My blood boils when politicians like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth treat our military like a political backdrop or talk about veterans' benefits as something to slash and privatize. Pete Hegseth and the political class in Washington love to wrap themselves in the flag, but when our service members come home broken, struggling, or needing care, they look the other way. They treat the men and women who put their lives on the line like line items on a spreadsheet instead of human beings who earned their care. Our troops and veterans don't need political posturing or lectures on culture wars from political appointees--they need a healthcare system that actually answers the phone when they call for help. I fought for this country for four decades, and I'm not going to sit quietly while politicians neglect the men and women who served alongside me. ~~ ~~ Thank you, Ret. Brigadier General Shawn Harris | ~~ "Facebook" ~ "X" \[BLUESKY\] "Bluesky" PAID FOR BY SHAWN FOR GEORGIA

**Chairman Maltzie Statement on Pappas and Goodlander’s Support of Socialism**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE****September 2nd, 2026**
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

**CONCORD, N.H.** — New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement on yesterday’s votes by Chris Pappas and Maggie Goodlander on a resolution condemning socialism:“This vote proves what Republicans have known all along: Chris Pappas and Maggie Goodlander are further left than they want Granite Staters to know,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “Chris Pappas voted against a resolution condemning socialism, which is baffling. He supports the DSA and its radical agenda, including its call to abolish the U.S. Senate, the very seat he is trying to win.”“Maggie Goodlander is no better. She voted ‘present’ on the resolution rather than taking a clear stand against socialism. Granite Staters deserve to know where these candidates stand and understand the consequences of sending politicians to Washington who refuse to take a stand against radical policies.”**Background:** H. Res. 1490, “Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes,” was voted on September 1st, 2026, with Roll Call 289.

name: Emily Berge
subject: Thank you!
body:
Hello Peter

I am reaching out to everyone who signed up to volunteer with my campaign.
Thank you so much for all the time and effort you put into the Berge for
Congress campaign. So many people have reached out to tell me that our
campaign inspired hope, and you all were a part of that. The energy we felt
was real and many people called the work we did "inspirational". Thank you
for being a part of this movement.

It's been almost three weeks since the primary. I have been busy processing
everything and spending time with my family. We dropped off our daughter at
college this past weekend so I have been soaking up time with her these
last few weeks (and dispensing last minute mom wisdom).

I think often about the people I connected with over the last 18 months
including all of our volunteers. I truly believe what we did mattered. We
built a community of people who wanted things to be different.

I have been thinking about how I can stay connected with this community we
built, and I decided to start "Political Therapy" — a newsletter and
podcast about the intersection of my life: politics and mental health. I
believe strong leadership needs the same honesty, compassion, and
authenticity that therapy requires.

If you want to stay connected, head to emilyberge.substack.com
<https://emily-berge.lmailroute.net/substack_die89xfy> and subscribe.
You'll get newsletters from me, plus links to the podcast as it launches,
and you'll get to see, in real time, where this community goes next.

Thank you again so much. I appreciate you.

~ Emily

|
Peter,
A whistleblower just confirmed that the USPS has been secretly building software to gut mail-in voting, in direct defiance of a court order blocking Trump's plan.
According to the whistleblower, a project like this normally takes nine months to a year. But this software was built in just a matter of weeks.
The system checks ballot barcodes against information uploaded by state election officials. If even just one bad barcode is detected, the entire batch gets rejected--upwards of ten thousand ballots getting rejected at once for each error.
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0012soFBRXYllgECbj46Y3tW0si4vWDGcScS9WgengOC0TusOidpCHV5g-FUQ1Rs8XVPI-hA0PS-Rs08yD6nj-WLhdKevV-IwULqNRrDBItQvF4d_LuHiqtSHxIKxOn1oEWxu7bc_puOjbUQbwT8EYy34Ex47pH-02qTVLg--ZYkoumcuMl1ByAgrHjbMlVqIYNm9eb_FoIWmAAIgZFHdRq3Fy2rUyD9rUu7eVKh5onlTdE2MYR8JouPA==&c=3EQclcWdAN3JY5Jmchw86r9nNk4hHzka6H_PrM3Ry4UIOrtOFYy8QQ==&ch=APg9LV7olw6Axzpg35CbaCi-RLRProvSdGpHhv5CUhUVhjNP2wLd0A==)
---
This complaint is not shocking. The system is not supposed to work, it is meant to fail on purpose. We all know mail-in ballots lean heavily Democratic. It's no surprise that the USPS software's "flaw" just so happens to be mass rejection of ballots over a single error.
Democrats have built our entire turnout operation around early and mail-in voting. We identify our voters, we knock on their doors, we call them, we get them to bank their ballot early. Once they vote, we move on to the next name on the list. It's incredibly effective at boosting turnout.
Republicans do the opposite. They wait until Election Day. That is why 2020 produced the "red mirage," Trump's early lead built on in-person votes, before Democrats surged ahead once mail-in ballots got counted.
Trump wants to break our best organizing tool and force Democrats to vote in person on Election Day, all while threatening to deploy ICE and the National Guard at polling locations and flooding the polls with over a thousand DOJ "election monitors" to intimidate voters and suppress turnout.
There is no doubt what Trump is trying to implement is unconstitutional. But with MAGA extremists controlling the Supreme Court, that may not matter. We just watched them gut the Voting Rights Act. We cannot rely on them saving us here.
That's why Defend Our Courts is preparing an emergency GOTV fund. On top of the budget already set aside for the next two months, we need a sizable reserve on hand so we can adapt our organizing strategy at a moment's notice.
We think Democrats everywhere need to be ready for the worst case scenario. Voters don't just need a plan to vote in this election, they need a backup plan too. If you typically vote by mail, be prepared to vote in person if it comes to that. That's what our emergency GOTV fund is for, to rapidly respond and get voters the information they need the moment things go south.
And it's why we're asking Democrats everywhere to pitch in to help fund it: Peter, [free and fair elections are under attack. Team Nunn ("JFC") is a joint fundraising committee composed of Iowans for Zach Nunn ("Campaign"), Call to Service PAC ("LPAC") and NRCC (each, a "Committee," and, collectively, the "Committees"). Any contribution to the JFC permissible under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended ("FECA"), from contributors who have not exceeded their applicable federal contribution limits, shall be allocated among the Committees pursuant to FECA and the formula set forth in this Notice.

_**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $7,000, designating up to $3,500 to the primary election and up to $3,500 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3\. NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $44,300 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

_**Contributions Made by a Federal Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $120,000. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $10,000, designating up to $5,000 to the primary election and up to $5,000 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3 .NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $15,000 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5 .NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

Contributions to Team Nunn, or to any participating Committee individually, are not deductible as charitable donations for federal income tax purposes. Contributions from corporations, labor organizations, national banks, federal government contractors, foreign nationals without green cards, and other federally impermissible sources are prohibited. The contributor's signature designates his or her contribution to the elections described above. Contributions that exceed a donor's contribution limit to a participating Committee shall be reallocated to the remaining Committees according to this allocation formula to the extent permitted by FECA. Any contributor may designate his or her contribution to a specific participant Committee to the extent permitted by FECA. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, mailing address, occupation, and name of employer of each individual whose aggregate contributions exceed $200 in an election cycle or calendar year, as applicable.

Hi, Peter – it’s Ken Burns.
Today, I’m asking you to make a donation to Roy Cooper’s campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. Winning this race is absolutely critical if we’re going to flip the Senate, so I hope you’ll join me in supporting Roy. [**_Will you chip in $5?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1276&amount=5&t=9&akid=3177%2E124072%2Ed9Cuh8)
Across this country, people are hurting in ways that don’t always make the history books but shape lives all the same.
The grocery bills that are too high. A lifesaving prescription that forces a difficult choice. A paycheck that just doesn’t stretch as far as it once did. | These are the real pressures that define a moment.
**Roy Cooper has spent much of his life as a public servant working to ease those burdens.**
Not seeking attention but doing the work. Expanding access to affordable health care. Investing in public schools. Defending the idea that government, at its best, is not distant but present, steady and accountable to the people it serves.
It is the kind of leadership that rarely makes noise, but over time, it leaves a mark.
Right now, there are those who want to take North Carolina – and our country – in a different direction. They see division as a strategy; they mistake power for purpose. They are organized. They are well-funded by dark-money and special-interest groups.
**The only way we can defeat them is if dedicated, caring people like you choose not to sit back but to take part. The power rests in our hands, and we must use it.**
[**_Will you make a donation of $5 or any amount today to help Roy flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1276&amount=5&t=10&akid=3177%2E124072%2Ed9Cuh8)

| | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. **Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him.** The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away.[**Will you help Sgt. Duran fight for his freedom?**](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=9faef22a166d449f901127e2edde8727&_e=3B8s7-mulSnnJSVUt0LAwtbtsP4XqVmeSQ8TfV94Pz1QGFVEFf-gCa8UwzXeDDVGdsNXOnaQt0Xk7frBmZq_Z8yi_LPD45DVH3lbtbZ0zQOGlPJwioJSJEDXUWHlNiklYx7Fj_ZjpPblaapdZE1A62CVybDSehU4dSx2eozEGZEpwLVB-l6mI1jjq5-wRwPCSTRolrWEteFfM-fsJe8lMb5AIWBhcMJDvWiQTK41haNDKu3b8KvpbgigTfrRgTaZMzJWuJY2d6RGJn0L87ENNV22oYnFHgi8wjbLoDgAl7929wUkixG7Wwcw66NKpENbkMmqt7hzP1Q8zzKiye8g1Pbhoa-plAuSStMtvH-gZ3k7lkJbozacNo48dyZOn42699ykMDcrhunCp7Ip88lJ7FX4k44MtjGbZ57O8Frn13xdZemgk2urPaWoMwwEvFTHhaUVVuviys3r71TqvrUMFltye7BWdvc-tjhHu5jlN4CrR1kUeKOJfGOk9tK27gMX7dxstlVAgxVObZ83fcoF0TQDvIsjy9BlGHg16u3oSdGfWHjUVeNebUkZb9UjPj91YkRFVstGQEBs5h0AFlPqXRKlNEGN32YO1X3NwiX_DM5UnaA13SkbQUDJrzYoO0_LJn19S_RmAN9anUc9n1qIV2i0f5LAckz184uhwVnB4UW1ZRG9zzW_gDjh1mqLav3q) The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. clean_body: Convicted because of a cooler Convicted because of a cooler | | | | | | Dear Fellow American,This officer was just convicted of manslaughter for trying to stop a fleeing criminal with non-lethal force. Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. Now he's fighting for his own freedom – All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx. | | - | | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him. The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away. The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. Duran and helping fund his appeal.But legal battles like this are long, difficult, and incredibly expensive.And while Erik fights for his freedom, his wife and children are left carrying the burden alongside him. They’re not only facing the reality of their husband and father spending the next 9 years in prison.Their own lives have been threatened because of this case. That's why I’m asking for your help today. spent 15 years protecting others. Now he needs people like you standing behind him. you for standing with Sgt. Duran. Sincerely, | | | Jason Johnson, President Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. To read more about our mission or the other Law Enforcement officers we're defending, please visit www.leldf.org. And remember - Blue Lives Matter! | | | | ---|---|---|--- © Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund | 2560 Huntington Ave. Suite 203, Alexandria, VA, 22303 Click |

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

First, four Republican-lite Democrats introduced an amendment in Congress
to condemn socialism and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

Then, two more so-called Democrats stepped out of line and voted with the
majority of Republicans to narrowly approve a rule change to bring this
amendment and other MAGA priorities, like the pro-voter suppression SAVE
Act, to a floor vote.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260902.iR_0Gs&refcode=em20260902-38225&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38225%2E1203867%2ECRM0Ce ]Tweet from @JakeSherman: "This has nothing to do with the CR. MGP and
Golden voted for a rule that would allow the House to vote on: 1) A bill
condemning socialism 2) Protecting Domestic Mining Act of 2025 3)
Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act of 2026 4) Protect Economic and
Academic Freedom Act of 2026 (prevents federally supported universities
from boycotting Israel)"

Now, the amendment passed with 8 Democrats voting for it, and we’re one
step closer to Republicans suppressing the right to vote for millions of
people.

What the actual f*ck are Democrats doing?

Trump and the GOP are attacking the right to vote ahead of the midterms,
and there are Congressmembers with D next to their name voting with them.

Republicans are lobbing ugly racist and Islamophobic attacks at blue
candidates before the general election, and these Democrats are more
worried about condemning progressive policies and candidates who want to
make life better for working people.

Fascism is here, Trump is defying court orders, ICE is still terrorizing
families, our food is increasingly unsafe to eat, people are dying of
measles, and families are struggling to survive the cost of living crisis...
and way too many Democrats would rather criticize the left flank of the
party than do something about any of it.

Justice Democrat, DSA member, and Congresswoman-elect Darializa Avila
Chevalier put it perfectly:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260902.iR_0Gs&refcode=em20260902-38225&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38225%2E1203867%2ECRM0Ce ]Tweet from @DarializaforNY: "Democrats love talking about a "big tent",
but then they vote in line with Republicans hell-bent on destroying our
democracy and stripping Black and brown people of the right to vote.
Tonight, some Democrats voted with Republicans to bring a resolution
condemning democratic socialism to the House floor, and then again to pass
it. This resolution was aimed squarely at democratic socialists like me,
paired with renewed support for the SAVE Act, a dangerous bill that would
require a passport or birth certificate to vote and could strip millions
of Americans, including Black voters and seniors without birth records, of
their right to vote."

Republicans have had no greater partners to enact their destructive agenda
than the corporate Dems who lead the Blue Dogs. Establishment Democrats
and Party leaders have proven time and again: they would rather attack the
bold ideas that their voters overwhelmingly demand than fight fascism and
oligarchy.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260902.iR_0Gs&refcode=em20260902-38225&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=38225%2E1203867%2ECRM0Ce ]We need to clean house until every Diet MAGA Democrat is out of office
and this party reflects the people it’s supposed to represent. Will you
pitch in $5 or more to help us elect three more progressive
champions to Congress this November?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260902.iR_0Gs&refcode=em20260902-38225&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=38225%2E1203867%2ECRM0Ce ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. In a video interview with the Washington, D.C.-based [POLITICO](https://substack.com/redirect/9ed34c3b-91b3-4f9e-99cb-ee7a7bb91ee3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), U.S. Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) made it clear that her re-election campaign will take the high road when it comes to her opponent's personal life.
In response to an inquiry about former Senate President Troy Jackson's non-marital consanguineous relationship that produced two children, Collins politely demurred.
"I'm not going to bring up the fact that the mother of his two children is his second cousin," Sen. Collins told POLITICO.
[(See the full interview here.)](https://substack.com/redirect/9ed34c3b-91b3-4f9e-99cb-ee7a7bb91ee3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jackson, who has claimed to live primarily in Allagash but also maintains a residence in Augusta, hasn't commented on the revelation that his co-parent partner is also his second cousin.

The pair have been keeping it in the family since at least 1988, when Fort Kent police records obtained by the Bangor newspaper recorded that Jackson burst into another man's home and violently assaulted the man, allegedly telling the man to stay away from his second cousin, Lana Pelletier.
The Robinson Report first reported exclusively on the interwoven nature of the Jackson family tree in July following a series of tips and a genealogical investigation.

In addition to being partners in consanguinity, Jackson and Pelletier also partnered to obtain a [Federal Housing Administration](https://substack.com/redirect/a318aa8a-54f5-4486-bec8-a804a1754345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) home loan.
Under the terms of the special low-interest FHA loan, Jackson agreed to make the home his primary residence -- which would have caused a conflict with his constitutional requirement to live within his northern Maine district.
In subsequent ethics proceedings, Jackson denied ever making the Augusta house his primary residence, effectively confessing to mortgage fraud.
He has not been charged.
In his defense, Jackson told the Portland newspaper that he never bothered reading the mortgage document, despite his initials appearing on each page.

6-minute read · 4 stories
Lead Story · IranU.S. STRIKES IRAN'S REVOLUTIONARY GUARD AS TRUMP WARNS OF "VERY LITTLE LEFT"What's Happening
* CENTCOM said Tuesday that U.S. forces completed a "wave of strikes" on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets across Iran, hitting **air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites**.
* President Trump said on Truth Social the strikes were retaliation for Iran's failed attempt to lay sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz and for missiles fired at a U.S. base in Jordan. He warned that if Tehran hits back, "there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran."
* Jordan's military said it intercepted **10 of 13** Iranian ballistic missiles; three landed in remote areas with no injuries or fatalities. Trump separately described an earlier salvo of eight missiles as "all successfully knocked down."
* A senior U.S. official told Fox News all American personnel are accounted for and there was no major damage to U.S. bases. CENTCOM said **more than 50,000 U.S. service members** remain deployed across the Middle East.
* Oil jumped roughly 4% to a one-week high: Brent rose $3.44 to **$93.93** and WTI rose $3.72 to **$89.48**.

The Situation
* The war has now passed six months. Tuesday's barrage was the second since Sunday night, following roughly a month with no U.S. airstrikes.
* Iranian state media reported a U.S. strike hit a wedding in Kuhestak, near the Strait, with Iranian officials putting the toll at at least five killed, including a child, and at least 68 wounded. CENTCOM spokesman Tim Hawkins said the command is aware of the reports and that the U.S. military does not target civilians. **These figures come from the Iranian government and have not been independently confirmed.**
* Trump said he is "not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table" and that an agreement with Tehran "isn't worth the paper it's written on."
* The senior U.S. official said Iran's command and control is not centralized and that "it remains unclear who within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is alive or dead."
* G20 finance ministers meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, called for "free, safe and predictable navigation" through the Strait of Hormuz. China formally objected to that paragraph.

The PerspectiveMining the Strait of Hormuz is not a grievance to be negotiated over. It is an attack on the shipping lanes the entire world depends on, and the administration is right that consequence is the only language Tehran has ever answered. But six months in, the bill is arriving at American gas pumps, and "waiting in the wings" is not a strategy anyone can hold a government accountable to. If this has become a sustained campaign rather than a series of responses, Congress should be asked to say so on the record — and the men flying the missions deserve a mission statement that outlasts a Truth Social post.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_N8M2yF9-VjcaxkG0L0zQSVmTJIXpgNSt33r0m9zLoxbGc4DLWZWXLh4yDGBWcCXph2aemFhdDyRVtO7mISHVVvjM70YHisiFQL63AC_6A6Ni8X1ZwihR0ljLlaYc0u8BqHK3vPchMMkva-I8RO9vWOKwFOLS3k9Ja6DIT6RmdftRas3xF-dWqGdRbXyAqviqunYtSL7-fp1cWMftDQVoei9yoPDBJ1qIrZVeNeiLqt6mzfYQRKeOmlrw7upyXdl4DrcESucIfKKEhc5T0zX5ojvJzAHwa8XZGzlsvIIQdx6nl4O0thXqZyUvXX6CzewyQ9JUcrdB2Uked-rILbc5-Y/4tp/uVLTZomzS4mkGh8VXSXHaQ/h6/h001.aZwzgA8IqTrg9mU15zspW9PLYCNlzmShpVzNDI5A-zA)

Government FundingHOUSE PASSES STOPGAP 370-48, PUNTING THE SPENDING FIGHT PAST THE ELECTIONWhat's Happening
* The House passed the Senate's continuing resolution Tuesday, **370-48** , funding the government at current levels through **Dec. 11** and sending it to the president's desk.
* It took **176 Democrats** to get there. **Nineteen Republicans** voted no.
* Leadership brought the bill up under suspension of the rules, which raises the passage threshold to two-thirds and made Democratic votes mathematically necessary.
* Democrats, who largely opposed a House GOP funding patch back in July, flipped over a federal grant provision and language blocking further transfers of money to **ICE and Border Patrol** beyond what the party-line budget bill approved earlier this year.
* The bill also delays a federal ban on intoxicating hemp products by just over four weeks — language written by Sens. Amy Klobuchar, Rand Paul and Jeff Merkley and added in the Senate in early August.

The Situation
* Rep. Keith Self (R-Texas), a no vote, on the suspension maneuver: "They've gone to get Democrat votes... They're not asking for my vote."
* Rep. Eric Burlison (R-Mo.) objected to the grants language, saying it would "cancel the ability for the administration to cancel these grants."
* Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) opposed the bill partly because it lacked language barring Medicaid reimbursements for abortion providers. Freedom Caucus Chairman Andy Harris (R-Md.) said the House should hold a separate vote on what he called the Senate's added provisions.
* The House has **14 legislative days** left before the November elections. The next funding cliff lands in the lame-duck session.
* The hemp ban's new effective date is reported inconsistently even within the coverage — the funding date is Dec. 11, but the hemp deadline is given variously as Dec. 11 and Dec. 12. Treat that specific date as unsettled.

The PerspectiveNo October shutdown three weeks before an election is a real win, and Republicans should bank it. But look at how it was won: a Republican majority funded the government using 176 Democratic votes, under a procedure that required them, with riders on hemp and federal grants that nobody campaigned on. Voters gave the GOP the gavel to set priorities, not to keep the lights on borrowed votes. Conservatives who are asking why a majority can't fund the government on its own terms are asking the right question — and December will ask it again.[Read the full story at Washington Examiner](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyWGzC9AGAjyTA5yLjEEj0SGMk56393XVlmKGvfeYIjzYm30_YYb6DIhF8cY4uwdG124rP9HX4Tju9CRL79mfoXcArdzM8tcAAy23xwRWmIsXLF1W2-PBh9k6pGTHercPBiT1Gyt36y1lZRribhQVWy_Kg20Lp8AphhrtV-BOgLg6mx-BCMkpm4GHUZAD1ZzP4tPxejeoSl9bquMQNWXg32KcIl45VYSlqOXMqHIfH2lGyd6ityTdkibAQzcEL-rUNjVnr0vmvJFiLLqyN2eD0RpzYK3OkqunxDeYYvf4HcKTMT_gpUcLrBfQoXvbGamvvbBZv-gwVY4HnFHjiXwwDUSpdHYN8-dHcqpqmvNrUq7Pw/4tp/uVLTZomzS4mkGh8VXSXHaQ/h7/h001._ns7hP0DLci9dA6XXCb0CO0_F4GjtdkFUvAGcHJZ31s)

Immigration EnforcementDHS REPORTS MORE THAN 2,100 NEW YORK ARRESTS, VOWS TO SEND "AS MANY PERSONNEL AS NECESSARY"What's Happening
* Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced results of **Operation Rotten Apple** at a Tuesday press conference at the USCIS New York field office.
* Mullin said the operation "has taken over 2,100 of the worst criminals off our streets statewide" over the last 30 days. DHS's own release puts the figure at **2,197 arrests between July 27 and Aug. 29**.
* Cases cited included a 39-year-old Indian national carrying an INTERPOL red notice tied to a rape charge in Germany, and a 50-year-old Ukrainian citizen with convictions including kidnapping, abduction, weapons possession and murder.
* Mullin said New York Democratic officials "have successfully lobbied for the release of over 13,000 illegal immigrants."
* He pledged escalation: "Because local leadership refuses to cooperate through the 287(g) program, we will send as many personnel as necessary to restore law and order."

The Situation
* Gov. Kathy Hochul terminated New York's 287(g) agreements, which had allowed local police to partner with ICE.
* Mullin took aim at Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has called ICE raids "cruel, inhumane, and do nothing to protect public safety."
* Hochul, at her own Tuesday press conference, accused the administration of "defunding the police," saying DHS is "withholding 40% of New York State's counterterrorism funding" — which she put at **$87 million**. Those are the governor's figures; DHS had not offered a counter-number by publication.
* Separately, the White House says "nearly 70% of illegal aliens arrested by ICE have been convicted or charged with a crime in the United States," pushing back on reporting that arrests of people with no criminal record are rising. **Both can be true at once** — a rising count of no-record arrests is compatible with a 70% share carrying U.S. charges.
* DHS has not published an offense-severity breakdown for the New York total, so the share of those 2,100-plus arrests involving violent offenders is not yet publicly verifiable.

The PerspectiveThere is no honest defense of turning a man with a murder conviction back onto a city street, and sanctuary policy forces federal agents to do door-to-door what a single phone call between agencies used to accomplish. That is the case for enforcement, and it is a strong one. Which is exactly why DHS should publish the offense breakdown instead of a rounded number. The argument does not need help from vague totals, and the credibility earned by releasing the data is worth more than the headline it might complicate.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NRx3TmKyUjNZ_2a-If6mrc497SYLc9u-Cka9a8syx7Al3Ji_t8bG4CLMSu-sKSeAQxjW7HkKPNmqLpV6H2JX0eFOduPA5EU7AyOlKc4ODuTaEed5w4Mlgcbj2DtE71pgDlPGXeQJjB70wNHt2uWew0HmYeUl1-ho-pcEEQvZPhh0YpGmx7JF4HeNENe9qvgaJb2rrAJuhIHQOcMFPUDs3plX5Cbqdvg7pY2skXouBmjRaw3OSTCryukC8yt9BUg6qjtKGv3g-ayJDQanJ2-EQ7kABvXnhTyKjxjcCueOmVO5sZ7Tdr1ZRVyzKk24I7lVloJFZcldfUjOVMCAlYXok8fyxMDbjhobFymsqOBO3QzTnsGdrJn_iKB6ckJgLn-9w/4tp/uVLTZomzS4mkGh8VXSXHaQ/h8/h001.yvcOO2eCq71YbCF5GVFyz86o0GDyYy7NdOVGyhhCZeU)

Election IntegrityANONYMOUS WHISTLEBLOWER HITS USPS BALLOT RULE AS COURTS RACE THE CALENDARWhat's Happening
* Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) released an anonymous whistleblower complaint, furnished by the nonprofit Whistleblower Aid, alleging USPS rushed its new **Federal Ballot Mail Portal** on an unrealistic timetable and failed to test it.
* The complaint's central claim: if "one bar code on one single ballot in a bulk-mailing of 10,000 ballots fails to properly scan during the verification process, the entire batch is rejected and sent back to the state."
* The final rule, published **Aug. 26** , requires official Election Mail markings, automation-compatible envelopes and unique Intelligent Mail barcodes on outbound and return federal ballot mail, and requires election offices to submit voter name, address, state and envelope barcodes through the portal.
* The Washington Examiner reports the published rule **does not establish** the zero-error threshold or the 10,000-ballot batch rejection the complaint describes — and that the complaint includes no testing results, no barcode-sampling standards, no emails, no source code and no record of USPS rejecting any ballot mailing.
* White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said building the verification software is "neither complex nor unique for USPS," which "regularly uses bulk mailing and intelligent mail barcodes for a wide variety of large customers."

The Situation
* **Twenty-four states and the District of Columbia** , along with voting organizations, sued after the rule was published. The Supreme Court had ruled the week before that an earlier challenge was premature because no final rule yet existed.
* The administration sought emergency relief from the 1st Circuit against U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani's 14-day block; the appeals court ordered plaintiffs to respond by 5 p.m. Tuesday, ahead of Talwani's Thursday preliminary-injunction hearing.
* The administration says it will not enforce the rule for November while a court order stands, but wants the standards available for the midterms and future federal elections.
* Hans von Spakovsky of Advancing American Freedom: "all of the whistleblower claims are very general and not specific enough to provide any real information on whether those claims are accurate."
* Stephen Richer, the former Maricopa County recorder now at Cato, called the compressed timeline "a major implementation challenge for USPS" while noting anonymous claims are inherently hard to assess.

The PerspectiveChain of custody for a ballot ought to be as boring and as verifiable as chain of custody for a package, and that is all a barcode requirement is. An anonymous complaint with no documents attached, describing a rejection mechanism the published rule does not actually contain, is thin ground for a national panic. But the same standard cuts both ways: a timeline this compressed is a real operational risk, and a vulnerability is not the same thing as proven fraud. President Trump said on Truth Social the strikes were retaliation for Iran's failed attempt to lay sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz and for missiles fired at a U.S. base in Jordan. He warned that if Tehran hits back, "there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran." Jordan's military said it intercepted 10 of 13 Iranian ballistic missiles; three landed in remote areas with no injuries or fatalities. Trump separately described an earlier salvo of eight missiles as "all successfully knocked down." A senior U.S. official told Fox News all American personnel are accounted for and there was no major damage to U.S. bases. CENTCOM said more than 50,000 U.S. service members remain deployed across the Middle East. Oil jumped roughly 4% to a one-week high: Brent rose $3.44 to $93.93 and WTI rose $3.72 to $89.48. Iranian state media reported a U.S. strike hit a wedding in Kuhestak, near the Strait, with Iranian officials putting the toll at at least five killed, including a child, and at least 68 wounded. CENTCOM spokesman Tim Hawkins said the command is aware of the reports and that the U.S. military does not target civilians. These figures come from the Iranian government and have not been independently confirmed. Trump said he is "not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table" and that an agreement with Tehran "isn't worth the paper it's written on." The senior U.S. official said Iran's command and control is not centralized and that "it remains unclear who within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is alive or dead." G20 finance ministers meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, called for "free, safe and predictable navigation" through the Strait of Hormuz. China formally objected to that paragraph. It is an attack on the shipping lanes the entire world depends on, and the administration is right that consequence is the only language Tehran has ever answered. If this has become a sustained campaign rather than a series of responses, Congress should be asked to say so on the record — and the men flying the missions deserve a mission statement that outlasts a Truth Social post. Government FundingHOUSE PASSES STOPGAP 370-48, PUNTING THE SPENDING FIGHT PAST THE ELECTIONWhat's Happening The House passed the Senate's continuing resolution Tuesday, 370-48 , funding the government at current levels through Dec. 11 and sending it to the president's desk. It took 176 Democrats to get there. Nineteen Republicans voted no. Leadership brought the bill up under suspension of the rules, which raises the passage threshold to two-thirds and made Democratic votes mathematically necessary. Democrats, who largely opposed a House GOP funding patch back in July, flipped over a federal grant provision and language blocking further transfers of money to ICE and Border Patrol beyond what the party-line budget bill approved earlier this year. The bill also delays a federal ban on intoxicating hemp products by just over four weeks — language written by Sens. Amy Klobuchar, Rand Paul and Jeff Merkley and added in the Senate in early August. The Situation Rep. Keith Self (R-Texas), a no vote, on the suspension maneuver: "They've gone to get Democrat votes... They're not asking for my vote." Rep. Eric Burlison (R-Mo.) objected to the grants language, saying it would "cancel the ability for the administration to cancel these grants." Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) opposed the bill partly because it lacked language barring Medicaid reimbursements for abortion providers. Freedom Caucus Chairman Andy Harris (R-Md.) said the House should hold a separate vote on what he called the Senate's added provisions. The House has 14 legislative days left before the November elections. The next funding cliff lands in the lame-duck session. The hemp ban's new effective date is reported inconsistently even within the coverage — the funding date is Dec. 11, but the hemp deadline is given variously as Dec. 11 and Dec. 12. Treat that specific date as unsettled. The PerspectiveNo October shutdown three weeks before an election is a real win, and Republicans should bank it. But look at how it was won: a Republican majority funded the government using 176 Democratic votes, under a procedure that required them, with riders on hemp and federal grants that nobody campaigned on. Voters gave the GOP the gavel to set priorities, not to keep the lights on borrowed votes. Conservatives who are asking why a majority can't fund the government on its own terms are asking the right question — and December will ask it again. Immigration EnforcementDHS REPORTS MORE THAN 2,100 NEW YORK ARRESTS, VOWS TO SEND "AS MANY PERSONNEL AS NECESSARY"What's Happening Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced results of Operation Rotten Apple at a Tuesday press conference at the USCIS New York field office. Mullin said the operation "has taken over 2,100 of the worst criminals off our streets statewide" over the last 30 days. DHS's own release puts the figure at 2,197 arrests between July 27 and Aug. 29. Cases cited included a 39-year-old Indian national carrying an INTERPOL red notice tied to a rape charge in Germany, and a 50-year-old Ukrainian citizen with convictions including kidnapping, abduction, weapons possession and murder. Mullin said New York Democratic officials "have successfully lobbied for the release of over 13,000 illegal immigrants." He pledged escalation: "Because local leadership refuses to cooperate through the 287(g) program, we will send as many personnel as necessary to restore law and order." The Situation Gov. Kathy Hochul terminated New York's 287(g) agreements, which had allowed local police to partner with ICE. Mullin took aim at Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has called ICE raids "cruel, inhumane, and do nothing to protect public safety." Hochul, at her own Tuesday press conference, accused the administration of "defunding the police," saying DHS is "withholding 40% of New York State's counterterrorism funding" — which she put at $87 million. Those are the governor's figures; DHS had not offered a counter-number by publication. Separately, the White House says "nearly 70% of illegal aliens arrested by ICE have been convicted or charged with a crime in the United States," pushing back on reporting that arrests of people with no criminal record are rising. Both can be true at once — a rising count of no-record arrests is compatible with a 70% share carrying U.S. charges. DHS has not published an offense-severity breakdown for the New York total, so the share of those 2,100-plus arrests involving violent offenders is not yet publicly verifiable. The PerspectiveThere is no honest defense of turning a man with a murder conviction back onto a city street, and sanctuary policy forces federal agents to do door-to-door what a single phone call between agencies used to accomplish. That is the case for enforcement, and it is a strong one. Which is exactly why DHS should publish the offense breakdown instead of a rounded number. The argument does not need help from vague totals, and the credibility earned by releasing the data is worth more than the headline it might complicate. Election IntegrityANONYMOUS WHISTLEBLOWER HITS USPS BALLOT RULE AS COURTS RACE THE CALENDARWhat's Happening Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) released an anonymous whistleblower complaint, furnished by the nonprofit Whistleblower Aid, alleging USPS rushed its new Federal Ballot Mail Portal on an unrealistic timetable and failed to test it. The complaint's central claim: if "one bar code on one single ballot in a bulk-mailing of 10,000 ballots fails to properly scan during the verification process, the entire batch is rejected and sent back to the state." The final rule, published Aug. 26 , requires official Election Mail markings, automation-compatible envelopes and unique Intelligent Mail barcodes on outbound and return federal ballot mail, and requires election offices to submit voter name, address, state and envelope barcodes through the portal. The Washington Examiner reports the published rule does not establish the zero-error threshold or the 10,000-ballot batch rejection the complaint describes — and that the complaint includes no testing results, no barcode-sampling standards, no emails, no source code and no record of USPS rejecting any ballot mailing. White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said building the verification software is "neither complex nor unique for USPS," which "regularly uses bulk mailing and intelligent mail barcodes for a wide variety of large customers." The administration says it will not enforce the rule for November while a court order stands, but wants the standards available for the midterms and future federal elections. Hans von Spakovsky of Advancing American Freedom: "all of the whistleblower claims are very general and not specific enough to provide any real information on whether those claims are accurate." When many of us were growing up, the stories we watched and read reinforced things like character, responsibility, and a basic understanding of where our country came from. Those stories weren't perfect--but they helped give us a sense of grounding.

Today, the media children are absorbing looks very different.

So much of what kids watch now either ignores America's history altogether or presents it in confusing and misleading ways. Children are forming their understanding of the world earlier than ever, and without a clear foundation, it's no wonder so many young adults today feel disconnected, uncertain, and adrift.

That's one of the reasons this project matters so much to me.

We're producing _Star Spangled Adventures: The Movie_ --a new film created specifically for children to help them understand America's story through engaging, clear, and inspiring storytelling. It's designed to be something families can watch together and trust.

As our nation approaches its 250th anniversary this year, I believe we have a responsibility to be intentional about the stories we pass on. What the next generation believes about our country, and about themselves, will be shaped by what they're taught today.

I'd like to invite you to take a simple pledge to stand with us.

When you take the pledge, you'll receive **exclusive behind-the-scenes sneak peeks of filming,** along with updates as the project moves forward and opportunities to help bring stories like this to life.

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

COCO’S TAX HEADS TO THE BALLOT AS BACKERS MOVE TO PULL INITIATIVE
175
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

For months, two transportation questions were headed toward the same
November ballot, pulling against each other. One would have locked
specified vehicle and fuel revenue to roads. The other would raise a
new tax to build a train. Within 24 hours, backers moved to pull one
as the district referred the other.

On Aug. 27, Restore Our Roads announced it would withdraw Initiative
175, the construction-industry measure that would have amended the
state constitution to reserve specified vehicle and fuel taxes and
fees for roads.

The next day, the Front Range Passenger Rail District board voted 14-1
at the Transportation Technology Center near Pueblo to send its own
funding question to voters. It asks for a 0.333% sales and use tax to
build the Colorado Connector, the intercity rail line branded CoCo.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

RIESS: GIVE RURAL PATIENTS MORE CHOICES, RURAL PROVIDERS MORE
FLEXIBILITY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY NAOMI RIESS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A Colorado House candidate lays out a bipartisan plan to expand rural
healthcare access by cutting red tape and empowering providers, not by
adding more one-size-fits-all mandates from Denver._

*
BUILDING ON BIPARTISAN MOMENTUM: Naomi Riess, a Republican candidate
for Colorado House District 59, proposes a Rural Colorado Primary Care
Access Act that builds on HB26-1096 — a bill letting Medicaid
patients voluntarily purchase direct primary care without losing
eligibility, which passed the House 40-22 with bipartisan support,
though she notes her opponent voted against it.

*
EXPANDING WHO CAN PROVIDE CARE: Riess argues Colorado should make it
easier for nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and certified
nurse midwives to serve rural areas to the full extent state law
safely allows, citing HB26-1092 on midwife privileges at public health
facilities — another bill her opponent voted to postpone
indefinitely.

*
CUTTING BUREAUCRACY, NOT ADDING IT: Her plan would direct state health
officials to identify and eliminate duplicative administrative
requirements burdening rural providers, while requiring any pilot
program to prove it actually improves access and reduces
emergency-room use before being expanded further.

_ Jason Green will take the hard questions. That is the pitch. The
co-founder and president of Raeden says his industry has never done a
good job showing up to answer for itself, so he has. “I’ve just
kind of held the mantle of that,” he said. In interviews before his
data center goes to the Colorado Springs City Council, he made himself
available for whatever anyone wanted to throw at him._

RECORDS FOR 11 DAYS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 29

_For 11 days in August, the profiles of Colorado voters who had
specifically asked the state to keep their information hidden were
searchable by anyone who knew where to look and had the information
the tool required._

__
__

__

THE RESOURCEFULNESS WEAPON: LITTLE BO-PEEP
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 29

_Poor Little Bo-Peep would have made a terrible investigator. Imagine
asking her a few basic questions: “Ma’am, when did you last see
your sheep? Did you search the pasture? Check the gate? Follow their
tracks? Talk to anyone who might have seen them?” Apparently, the
answer to all of the above would have been no. Her investigative
strategy was much simpler: Leave them alone, and they’ll come home._

Dear Patriot, **In just one month, we're taking our message straight to the Library of Congress.** On September 26, I will kick off this year's "See You at the Library" Story Hours at America's Library in Washington, D.C. Then, just one week later, something truly incredible will happen. Christian parents and grandparents across America will walk into their local public libraries with their children and grandchildren. And in a matter of hours, hundreds of Story Hours will fill children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. This is our chance to bring God's truth into libraries across America and reach an entire generation of children. **This year, honoring America's 250th birthday, our ambitious goal is to expand "See You at the Library Day" to reach 250,000 children.** **And we are just ONE MONTH away.** Before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host "Story Hours" has been overwhelming. But it's going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold "Story Hours" for 250,000 children. **And with just over one month left, the clock is running out to fund the Story Hours we need to reach 250,000 children.** **[That's why I'm asking you to rush back your tax-deductible sponsorship gift of $35, $50, $125, $250 or more today.](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=8244502913fa43be90903e72cb61fffb&_e=-ch2auAwUFNdviYGvnWuz_CBI3vkrWw9Hno7un2joiLDpz-8TcNZo20IVwirLym8NJpmadECA4dg6QPYcnAXy0FZtHwQDps4SNr1pOsN_zBZBbHBR6yefwikvLPVGJjKdXhX1C6rmO3_2gC0rP5vOwla0QFGR0TyYdGZg5fvk2tlp1tK78IGwLEI4swCzIR876fg2nGU8hZ6_EFNbSkUxLfR3p0uTkMn5ne1d9t9w72GsfaY4nhnQVKAPNLqTE6BVOcm3DRg65xikHR3ehdBZyBpsGfqvspAFlTBERiapzMGE6lC4IYepedgmvUgh3-FAv_GxbywFELpk5rp1ujvvZqyONA-OcixfknsxMh67AU03Jyr8zqb5bM8-A1r7MOb06jLMv1aKoDKteyhp8l9JEwNc2QbdeH1mOR0soPBol9mPqJTybsMTQ_uamNy8-JrzRk9uUG_F0gc5WP7aUVojpIBM08pEc1cN2UCGN-ahXqByYdiCcKcqZkp56KS3D2mKy_5zVw5A5iR2LQ3IKhZJPKGbiuKvuaEagFaHBg_OpgO7xNW21zTxE3GX5YAcdTZnYo6zCkAOwdG1-5IMWK-zvDWpEsqtaB-5L7OUBUi7DIRH9PCf4bXqD0rX9mXB0gtaHEaYyY4Q5oKKwCfWnO3z8uURbq5MFrxCfhD4DkqHvVltm_AoXQ9f9F05k49frIV)** Friend, America's children need to hear our message because today's "educators" and librarians are radicals! Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. clean_body: In just one month, we're taking our message straight to the Library of Congress. | | | | Dear Patriot, In just one month, we're taking our message straight to the Library of Congress. On September 26, I will kick off this year's "See You at the Library" Story Hours at America's Library in Washington, D.C. Then, just one week later, something truly incredible will happen. Christian parents and grandparents across America will walk into their local public libraries with their children and grandchildren. And in a matter of hours, hundreds of Story Hours will fill children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. This is our chance to bring God's truth into libraries across America and reach an entire generation of children. This year, honoring America's 250th birthday, our ambitious goal is to expand "See You at the Library Day" to reach 250,000 children. And we are just ONE MONTH away. Before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host "Story Hours" has been overwhelming. But it's going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold "Story Hours" for 250,000 children. And with just over one month left, the clock is running out to fund the Story Hours we need to reach 250,000 children. Friend, America's children need to hear our message because today's "educators" and librarians are radicals! Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like Pat the Bunny and The Little Engine That Could. But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, radical activists have worked to turn our public libraries into vehicles for their values. But we can't just sit back and complain about it. We're countering those awful "Drag Queen Story Hours" with conservative Story Hours filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism. And on October 3, a little boy or girl will stand up at their public library as straight and tall as they possibly can... ...as their right hand covers their heart, and they proudly pledge allegiance to our American flag. We'll teach them: Freedom Requires Courage. Great Blessings Require Great Sacrifice. IN GOD WE TRUST. And we hope to engrave those lessons on every child's heart at "See You at the Library Day." But first, we have to get the resources into the hands of the parents, grandparents, and patriots who are organizing these Story Hours. News recently broke about Hegseth employing right-wing influencers as “special government employees” at the Pentagon. These are people on Twitter and other platforms enlisted by the Pentagon to attack whoever and post whatever Hegseth tells them to.

Hey folks,
This one is absolutely wild. Laura Loomer and Milo Yiannopoulos are tearing each other apart--and somehow their personal MAGA feud has collided with the power of the federal government.
Milo is out of the country. Loomer's influence is under the microscope. And underneath all the chaos is a much bigger question about power, empathy, and what happens when personal vendettas start shaping government action.
* [**00:00:55**] Milo gets deported after overstaying his visa--and suddenly says he regrets supporting Donald Trump.
* [**00:03:31**] We get into the part that actually matters: empathy, due process, and why you don't have to like someone to care about how government power gets used.
* [**00:05:52**] A look back at Milo's history, the controversy that cost him his CPAC invitation and book deal, and why I'm not interested in rewriting who he is.
* [**00:09:32**] The bigger Laura Loomer problem: what happens when someone with no elected position appears to wield extraordinary influence over people inside the federal government?
* [**00:12:32**] The MAGA civil war is getting uglier--and I think this fight tells us something important about the battle already underway for 2028.

This isn't really a story about feeling sorry for Milo. It's about whether we still believe in rules, checks and balances, and a government that doesn't become a weapon for settling personal scores. It's also about a MAGA movement increasingly turning on itself as everyone fights over what comes after Trump. **If you value independent media willing to expose this stuff without surrendering our empathy in the process, help me keep building it.**
