body:
Republicans can gerrymander Florida, but they can’t stop voters from showing up and fighting back at the polls.
#
Hi there,
Swing Left recently announced that we’re expanding our 2026 target map to include 6 new U.S. House districts in our “Must-Flip” and “Must-Hold” categories.
**Today, we’re taking a closer look at the 3 newly added Florida U.S. House seats that are absolutely imperative to protect this fall.**
Earlier this year, Governor Ron DeSantis and Florida Republicans rammed through an aggressive mid-decade gerrymander designed to wipe out Democratic representation and protect Republicans’ razor-thin majority in the U.S. House.
To pull off this power grab, Republicans specifically redrew the districts of three Democratic incumbents in Central Florida, the Tampa Bay region, and South Florida. But their strategy has a major vulnerability: Trump’s 2024 performance in these newly drawn districts overstates how Republican they actually are.
With Trump’s popularity dropping across the state, these three incumbents are uniquely positioned to hold their seats and defeat the GOP's gerrymander.
**Florida’s 9th Congressional District: Representative Darren Soto**
Republicans redrew Florida’s 9th Congressional District, making the new seat one that Trump would have won by 18% in 2024. But, if the newly drawn district boundaries had been in place for the 2020 presidential election, Trump would’ve won this district by just 6.8%. Florida’s 9th is also nearly one-third Hispanic—a key constituency swinging back to Democrats after seeing the impact of Republican policies.
Democratic Representative Darren Soto is a high-performing incumbent who consistently outperforms top-of-the-ticket Democrats by delivering results for Central Florida, from securing disaster relief to fighting for lower healthcare costs to banning congressional stock trading.
His challenger, Republican Dan Green, is a multimillionaire rubber-stamp for D.C. elites who supports tariff hikes that raise homebuilding costs and healthcare cuts that threaten coverage for over 1.6 million Floridians.
**Florida’s 14th Congressional District: Representative Kathy Castor**
GOP mapmakers reshaped Tampa Bay, making this district one that Trump would have won by 10.5% in 2024, but again, if the newly drawn district boundaries had been in place for the 2020 presidential election, the margin would have been a razor-thin 2.8%. Independent analyst Cook Political Report currently rates this race as a Toss-Up.
Democratic Representative Kathy Castor is a deeply trusted leader who has spent her career lowering costs for Tampa families, fighting utility monopolies, and securing billions in federal infrastructure investments.
In comparison, her opponent, Republican Mike Beltran, is an extreme conservative who voted against state affordable housing packages, supported a near-total abortion ban, and backs national policies that are estimated to add thousands to the average family's annual budget.
**Florida’s 25th Congressional District: Representative Jared Moskowitz**
Republicans redrew this seat to make it more Republican-leaning, but with these new lines, Joe Biden would have won this district by 5.1% in 2020. Independent analyst Cook Political Report currently rates this race as a Toss-Up.
Democratic Representative Jared Moskowitz is a pragmatic problem-solver who has recovered nearly $25 million for local taxpayers and introduced legislation to curb soaring property insurance rates.
His opponent, Scott Singer, is a wealthy former mayor who supports healthcare cuts and tariffs that crush South Florida seniors and working families.
**How You Can Help**
Republicans rigged Florida maps because they know they can’t win on the issues alone. But these races are still winnable. Gerrymandered maps can’t stop Floridians from turning out in force in these three districts and making their voices heard at the ballot box.
By organizing early and funding ground operations in Florida’s 9th, Florida’s 14th, and Florida’s 25th, we can protect these Democratic incumbents, fight back against Republicans’ efforts to lock in power they couldn’t win under fair maps, and pave the way to a Democratic House majority.
That’s why we need to scale up Ground Truth, our innovative, people-powered deep canvassing program in Florida and in swing districts across the country, to listen, understand what voters truly care about, and make that information available to Democrats to build winning campaigns.
Getting volunteers on the ground and across the country will take resources. **[Will you donate $25 to support Ground Truth and defend critical House races across the country?](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl-em20260902.-e014k&refcode=em20260902-2651&amount=25&t=1&akid=2651%2E1562180%2En7POkK)**

Thank you for being part of this work.
— The Swing Left Team
**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. Hi there, Swing Left recently announced that we’re expanding our 2026 target map to include 6 new U.S. House districts in our “Must-Flip” and “Must-Hold” categories. Today, we’re taking a closer look at the 3 newly added Florida U.S. House seats that are absolutely imperative to protect this fall. Earlier this year, Governor Ron DeSantis and Florida Republicans rammed through an aggressive mid-decade gerrymander designed to wipe out Democratic representation and protect Republicans’ razor-thin majority in the U.S. House. To pull off this power grab, Republicans specifically redrew the districts of three Democratic incumbents in Central Florida, the Tampa Bay region, and South Florida. But their strategy has a major vulnerability: Trump’s 2024 performance in these newly drawn districts overstates how Republican they actually are. With Trump’s popularity dropping across the state, these three incumbents are uniquely positioned to hold their seats and defeat the GOP's gerrymander. Florida’s 9th Congressional District: Representative Darren Soto Republicans redrew Florida’s 9th Congressional District, making the new seat one that Trump would have won by 18% in 2024. But, if the newly drawn district boundaries had been in place for the 2020 presidential election, Trump would’ve won this district by just 6.8%. Florida’s 9th is also nearly one-third Hispanic—a key constituency swinging back to Democrats after seeing the impact of Republican policies. Democratic Representative Darren Soto is a high-performing incumbent who consistently outperforms top-of-the-ticket Democrats by delivering results for Central Florida, from securing disaster relief to fighting for lower healthcare costs to banning congressional stock trading. His challenger, Republican Dan Green, is a multimillionaire rubber-stamp for D.C. elites who supports tariff hikes that raise homebuilding costs and healthcare cuts that threaten coverage for over 1.6 million Floridians. Florida’s 14th Congressional District: Representative Kathy Castor GOP mapmakers reshaped Tampa Bay, making this district one that Trump would have won by 10.5% in 2024, but again, if the newly drawn district boundaries had been in place for the 2020 presidential election, the margin would have been a razor-thin 2.8%. Independent analyst Cook Political Report currently rates this race as a Toss-Up. Democratic Representative Kathy Castor is a deeply trusted leader who has spent her career lowering costs for Tampa families, fighting utility monopolies, and securing billions in federal infrastructure investments. In comparison, her opponent, Republican Mike Beltran, is an extreme conservative who voted against state affordable housing packages, supported a near-total abortion ban, and backs national policies that are estimated to add thousands to the average family's annual budget. Florida’s 25th Congressional District: Representative Jared Moskowitz Republicans redrew this seat to make it more Republican-leaning, but with these new lines, Joe Biden would have won this district by 5.1% in 2020. Independent analyst Cook Political Report currently rates this race as a Toss-Up. Democratic Representative Jared Moskowitz is a pragmatic problem-solver who has recovered nearly $25 million for local taxpayers and introduced legislation to curb soaring property insurance rates. His opponent, Scott Singer, is a wealthy former mayor who supports healthcare cuts and tariffs that crush South Florida seniors and working families. How You Can Help Republicans rigged Florida maps because they know they can’t win on the issues alone. But these races are still winnable. Gerrymandered maps can’t stop Floridians from turning out in force in these three districts and making their voices heard at the ballot box. By organizing early and funding ground operations in Florida’s 9th, Florida’s 14th, and Florida’s 25th, we can protect these Democratic incumbents, fight back against Republicans’ efforts to lock in power they couldn’t win under fair maps, and pave the way to a Democratic House majority. That’s why we need to scale up Ground Truth, our innovative, people-powered deep canvassing program in Florida and in swing districts across the country, to listen, understand what voters truly care about, and make that information available to Democrats to build winning campaigns. Getting volunteers on the ground and across the country will take resources. name: Seth Moulton
subject: Thank you
body:
I'm proud of the race we ran together.

| |
---
Friend, We always knew we were the underdog in this race, but that doesn’t mean it wasn’t a fight worth taking on. We ran a race that stood on principle – that wasn’t just about politics as usual – and that elevated the voices of Massachusetts citizens who have been left behind by the status quo in Washington. I am proud of the race we ran, the culture our campaign built, and the conversations we started. Challenging the establishment and calling for a new generation of leadership isn’t easy, but it is necessary. I am confident that, because of this campaign, others will be inspired to buck the system when they’re told to wait their turn. And I will continue to push the Democratic Party – and our country – to look towards the future. I spoke to Senator Markey last night and pledged to help him win re-election in November, to ensure a Democrat represents the state we both love, and I will continue to fight to elect Democrats across the country. Thank you to everyone who knocked doors, made calls, donated, hosted us, showed up at town halls, and trusted me with your vote. You gave this campaign everything we needed to compete, and I am deeply grateful. Thank you for being with me. Seth
| | |
---|---|---

Seth Moulton is a Marine and a Democrat with a mission to bring a new generation of leaders to Congress. Seth’s two young daughters, Emmy and Caroline, remind him every day why new leadership and urgent action can’t wait any longer.

clean_body: | | | Republicans are getting nervous, Peter. After a new poll showed WFP champion Will Lawrence up by just 2 points over the Republican incumbent in MI-07, House Speaker Mike Johnson told Republican donors that this a top-priority.1 In a district that Trump won by just 1% in 2024, he knows that this is set to be one of the closest races in the country and is key to the GOP maintaining their slim majority. And he knows that as Will reaches more voters with his commitment to protect our communities from data centers, lower the cost of living, and say no to endless wars — we have a real opportunity to flip this seat and send a real movement progressive to Congress. Will Lawrence is the kind of leader who is unafraid to fight for what we deserve. As data centers force their way into our towns and neighborhoods, sucking up our resources and making our utility bills even more unaffordable, Will is refusing to let Silicon Valley billionaires bully us. Meanwhile, Will’s opponent has taken huge amounts of money from tech billionaires after voting for $83 billion in tax breaks for data centers.2 Now, he’s desperately scrambling to re-write his own history of supporting AI companies as voters from across the aisle are increasingly turning against the wasteful, expensive, and environmentally destructive data centers. Mike Johnson knows his slim majority is in jeopardy, Peter, and this race may just be the one that flips the House. But with MAGA Super PACs already pledging to spend millions to defeat Will in the fall, this is going to be a close one. Help us drown out the Republican noise and fearmongering and replace a far-right incumbent with a visionary WFP champion. | | | I need your help answering some questions, Peter:
---
**_Why did my opponent give his first interview to a Florida podcaster, Matt Gaetz, not to a local newspaper?_** **_Why did he joke about his own past $5 Venmo payments labeled “the strippers” and “high supplies”? _** **_And why haven’t I seen him at events or even agree to one debate?_**

Sorry, Hillary. I didn't vote for you.
Solely being a woman isn't a qualification for leadership.
Peter, I've had some stuff on my mind and it feels really good to get it off my chest.
I'm sure you know by now that I've recently walked away from a career I loved. Plenty of people call me crazy for it. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line._
_Especially in my beloved Minnesota.
Right now, parents who speak up are being called transphobes. Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet. And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
It's terrible.
That's why I've taken a huge leap of faith. I want my daughter and every young girl and boy across the country to know this:
1) You earn your place 2) You think for yourself 3) You never let anyone put you in a box
That's exactly what I'm fighting for.
It's not rocket science. GIRLS' sports are for GIRLS.
And if you are to remember one thing about me let it be this: I will not apologize for taking a stand. At the end of the day, if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, I've done my job.
Now, the contingent of people on the radical Left who have been pushing this ideology tirelessly on us will stop at absolutely nothing.
Whether I face Peggy Flanagan or Angie Craig, I'm going up against a far-Left, extremist who will vote to allow boys competing against girls in sports, block voter ID requirements, open up our borders, raise your taxes, and sabotage anything the President wants to do.

I'm far from a career politician. My campaign is focused on honesty, common sense, stopping fraud, and doing the small things right.
That's why we need to win. Failure here is not an option.
And without your help, Peter... we will never cut through the far Left's propaganda machine to get our message out.

clean_body: Solely being a woman isn't a qualification for leadership. | Sorry, Hillary. I didn't vote for you. Solely being a woman isn't a qualification for leadership. Peter, I've had some stuff on my mind and it feels really good to get it off my chest. I'm sure you know by now that I've recently walked away from a career I loved. Plenty of people call me crazy for it. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line. Especially in my beloved Minnesota. Right now, parents who speak up are being called transphobes. Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet. And women's groups are nowhere to be found. It's terrible. That's why I've taken a huge leap of faith. I want my daughter and every young girl and boy across the country to know this: 1) You earn your place 2) You think for yourself 3) You never let anyone put you in a box That's exactly what I'm fighting for. It's not rocket science. GIRLS' sports are for GIRLS. And if you are to remember one thing about me let it be this: I will not apologize for taking a stand. At the end of the day, if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, I've done my job. Now, the contingent of people on the radical Left who have been pushing this ideology tirelessly on us will stop at absolutely nothing. Whether I face Peggy Flanagan or Angie Craig, I'm going up against a far-Left, extremist who will vote to allow boys competing against girls in sports, block voter ID requirements, open up our borders, raise your taxes, and sabotage anything the President wants to do. I'm far from a career politician. My campaign is focused on honesty, common sense, stopping fraud, and doing the small things right. That's why we need to win. Failure here is not an option. And without your help, Peter... we will never cut through the far Left's propaganda machine to get our message out. | | | | | | | | I can't do this without you. I mean that. Be brave. Do good.- Michele Michele TafoyaRepublican for Senate, Minnesota Hey folks - it's Michele. You need to see this Minnesota Senate poll. It has me STATISTICALLY TIED with Peggy Flanagan! The far-Left must 've been furious when they saw this. They've controlled Minnesota for decades, and now a political outsider is within the margin of error! We have the opportunity of a LIFETIME to win back this Senate seat in the name of sanity. Forgive my bluntness, but I'm hoping everyone reading this can send at least 15 dollars. If you're able to give more, even better. But this race will be decided by the slimmest of margins, so it'll take ALL OF US doing our part to win. | | | Paid for by Tafoya for Senate 3500 Vicksburg LN N, STE 267, Plymouth, MN 55447

I like to begin the Good Trouble Report each week with a word from John Lewis. The report's title is his doing, in a sense. Lewis made it his life's work to tell us that history can be altered by ordinary people when they put their minds to it. Not the politicians, not the powerful, not the famous. But you and me when we're willing to get into some necessary, righteous trouble.
This week's nominee has taken that lesson to heart. And in doing so, they've shown a level of courage that comes at a real price. We don't know who they are. What we do know is that on Monday, an anonymous whistleblower inside the United States Postal Service put something on the record that every American who cares about their vote needs to hear.
Standing Our Ground is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..BDoEl76t6P2xlBsW_0u2uN_b1V4eySgfWeHLou1rZcU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=213923350)
The Trump administration has been pressuring the Postal Service to build a brand-new computer system for verifying mail ballots ahead of the November midterms. This whistleblower went straight to Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut with a complaint: the system is a shoddy affair, riddled with errors, and it's liable to fail in a catastrophic way when it counts most.
Here's how bad it is. A system like this normally takes over a year to build correctly. The USPS started this one around June 15th. Three months. That's all they've given themselves to construct something that will decide whether millions of Americans receive their ballot in time to vote.
And then there's this: a federal judge had already put a temporary block on Trump's executive order limiting mail voting. The administration appealed it. But according to the whistleblower, the Postal Service may have kept right on building this system anyway, potentially defying that court order in the process. Put plainly: the Trump administration may have ignored a federal judge, continued building a broken system behind closed doors, and is counting on no one noticing before November.
I noticed. And you should too.
Senator Blumenthal has since written to the Postmaster General to put him on notice. I'm grateful for that. But I'll be watching closely, because a strongly worded letter is not enough. This moment calls for oversight with real teeth. Accountability that actually means something.
What this whistleblower did took guts. We're not talking about filing a routine complaint. This person works inside a federal agency controlled by an administration that has made abundantly clear it will bring the full weight of government down on anyone who stands in its way. We've seen the retaliation. We've seen the investigations. We've seen what happens to people who speak up. This person knew all of that. They knew their identity could be exposed. They knew what comes with it... the harassment, the threats, the targeting.
And they came forward anyway.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..BDoEl76t6P2xlBsW_0u2uN_b1V4eySgfWeHLou1rZcU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=213923350)
If you're reading this and you're that person, thank you. You did something that most people never find the nerve to do. You saw something wrong, and you said something. You got into good trouble.
The right to vote is the foundation of everything else in this democracy. It is the most powerful tool ordinary Americans have. When that tool is being quietly sabotaged, technically, in ways most people won't notice until it's too late -- that is not a bureaucratic error. That is an attack on democracy itself.
We have to pay attention. We have to stay loud. And we have to make sure the people willing to risk everything to tell us the truth know that we are listening.
That's what the Good Trouble Report is for.
Keep getting in good trouble.
-- Harry

# Adelante con Adelita💙🌵
Adelita for Congress Newsletter
---
| | Hi Peter,

We want to pause to address the recent tragic shooting at Venture-N. Our hearts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected. Our campaign and Congresswoman stand unconditionally with the LGBTQ+ community, and we remain fully committed to fostering spaces safe from hate.
**As Adelita stated,****“** _**I am disgusted and deeply saddened to learn of a targeted act of hate and the cold-blooded murder of two members of our LGBTQIA+ community, Vincent Siqueiros and Cameron Capara, at the Venture-N bar in Tucson last night. This horrific attack is a painful reminder that even in welcoming communities like Tucson, hate and violence against the LGBTQIA+ community still exist.”**_
_**“When that hate is combined with easy access to firearms, the consequences can be deadly. I am sick and tired of Congress refusing to lift a finger to protect our communities while, every day, dozens of people are shot and killed across the country. It does not have to be this way. The House of Representatives is returning to session this week, and our first action should be passing common-sense gun safety reforms that we know can save lives.”**_
_**“In Tucson, we must come together as one city, mourn alongside the victims’ families and friends, and stand with our LGBTQIA+ community in saying in the most unconditional terms: everyone is welcome in Tucson, and hate has no place here.”**_
We will continue to stand along with our LGBTQ+ community and continue to fight, which is why we need to send Adelita back to Congress. Sign up down below, lets continue this fight!

Peter, President Obama and I founded the National Democratic Redistricting Committee as the first-ever strategic hub for the fair maps movement **because we needed to address a crisis that was getting out of hand.** Across the country, Republicans had gone out of their way to abuse the redistricting process and manipulate maps to steal power they didn’t earn. These guys didn’t invent gerrymandering. But it sure seemed like they were trying to perfect it. They engineered themselves an obscene 47-seat structural advantage in the U.S. House, which let them keep control even after losing the popular House vote in 2012. **President Obama and I believe that when the maps are fair, democracy works the way it’s supposed to. So we fought back.** The fair maps movement achieved incredible results in just a few short years. By the last midterm election in 2022, we were competing on what _The New York Times_ called “the fairest House map of the last 40 years.” **When Donald Trump instigated a national crisis of mid-decade redistricting, he did so as a direct and extreme response to the progress you and I have fought for. These Republican extremists believe it's their right to cheat — that power belongs to them, not the American people.
And, enabled by the Supreme Court’s radical ruling gutting the Voting Rights Act this year, they’ve instituted a modern-day, politicalJim Crow, with new maps that deprive Black and brown Americans of fair and equal representation. It’s nothing short of racial discrimination.
**I spoke to President Obama the other day about how we respond in this moment, how we stop this power grab, and how we ultimately repair our democracy for good.**
We must run the table in the most important state-level elections this fall — where we have endorsed over 200 Democracy Defenders. They stand ready to hold the line for fair maps, fair elections, and the right to vote.
We must build power in the places where the next redistricting fights are bound to crop up, so we can keep Republicans from continuing to tilt the playing field in their favor.

clean_body: I’m asking for your continued support | Peter, President Obama and I founded the National Democratic Redistricting Committee as the first-ever strategic hub for the fair maps movement because we needed to address a crisis that was getting out of hand. Across the country, Republicans had gone out of their way to abuse the redistricting process and manipulate maps to steal power they didn’t earn. These guys didn’t invent gerrymandering. But it sure seemed like they were trying to perfect it. They engineered themselves an obscene 47-seat structural advantage in the U.S. House, which let them keep control even after losing the popular House vote in 2012. President Obama and I believe that when the maps are fair, democracy works the way it’s supposed to. So we fought back. The fair maps movement achieved incredible results in just a few short years. By the last midterm election in 2022, we were competing on what The New York Times called “the fairest House map of the last 40 years.” When Donald Trump instigated a national crisis of mid-decade redistricting, he did so as a direct and extreme response to the progress you and I have fought for. He’s gotten his party to manipulate more maps in their favor because they are too frightened to face the voters in a free and fair election. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = These Republican extremists believe it's their right to cheat — that power belongs to them, not the American people. And, enabled by the Supreme Court’s radical ruling gutting the Voting Rights Act this year, they’ve instituted a modern-day, politicalJim Crow, with new maps that deprive Black and brown Americans of fair and equal representation. It’s nothing short of racial discrimination. I spoke to President Obama the other day about how we respond in this moment, how we stop this power grab, and how we ultimately repair our democracy for good. We must run the table in the most important state-level elections this fall — where we have endorsed over 200 Democracy Defenders. We must build power in the places where the next redistricting fights are bound to crop up, so we can keep Republicans from continuing to tilt the playing field in their favor. Frankly, I would like to make the U.S.-Canada relationship boring again.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138456807/644107953/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZjIzNDc2Mi0xYmE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PSBB9e2AVXt8o9FxbcAWKVtuKnHJ7ndImiOmrxntJ4s=&emci=6b638ae4-0da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=bf234762-1ba7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=9494239)

| | **The Trump administration imposed new 50 percent tariffs on approximately $50 billion worth of Canadian goods.** This follows the collapse of trade negotiations between the United States and Canada and represents another major disruption to one of America's most important economic relationships. So, what does this mean for Northwest Washington? **First, tariffs can raise prices.** A tariff is essentially a tax on imported goods. When businesses have to pay more to bring products into the United States, those higher costs can move through the supply chain and affect consumers. That matters in Northwest Washington, where families are already working to manage the rising cost of gas, groceries, housing, and other essentials. **Second, our economy depends on a stable relationship with Canada.** Over the past year, my office has held more than 100 meetings and conversations with farmers, businesses, municipalities, ports and other stakeholders across Northwest Washington. I heard a consistent message: a stable economic relationship with Canada and Mexico is critical to keeping local businesses afloat, lowering costs, and creating good-paying jobs. Our region's farmers, manufacturers, ports, and other businesses depend on being able to trade reliably across the border. When trade policy changes abruptly and negotiations break down, that uncertainty has real consequences for workers and businesses here at home. **Third, this could make a trade agreement that has worked for Northwest Washington less effective.** For years, the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, known as USMCA, provided a framework for trade among the three countries. Many goods that were protected from import taxes under that agreement are now subject to these new tariffs. In July, I sent a report to the U.S. Trade Representative outlining what I heard from people across Northwest Washington and urging the continuation of USMCA. I have also worked with my colleagues on the New Democrat Coalition Trade and Tariffs Task Force to call for the agreement to be renewed and strengthened. There is still disagreement over why the latest negotiations between the United States and Canada broke down. But there should be no disagreement about the importance of getting our economic relationship back on stable ground. Canada is our neighbor, our ally, and one of our most important trading partners. As the top Democrat on the U.S.-Canada Interparliamentary Group, I have seen firsthand how much both countries benefit when we work together to solve shared challenges. The bottom line is simple: trade can create jobs and lower costs. Reckless tariffs can do the opposite. **I will keep working to end these tariffs, bring down costs for families and businesses, and restore a stable economic relationship with Canada.** And, frankly, I would like to make the U.S.-Canada relationship boring again. _Rick_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Rick Larsen instantly:

clean_body: Frankly, I would like to make the U.S.-Canada relationship boring again. | | | | The Trump administration imposed new 50 percent tariffs on approximately $50 billion worth of Canadian goods. This follows the collapse of trade negotiations between the United States and Canada and represents another major disruption to one of America's most important economic relationships. So, what does this mean for Northwest Washington? First, tariffs can raise prices. A tariff is essentially a tax on imported goods. When businesses have to pay more to bring products into the United States, those higher costs can move through the supply chain and affect consumers. That matters in Northwest Washington, where families are already working to manage the rising cost of gas, groceries, housing, and other essentials. Second, our economy depends on a stable relationship with Canada. Over the past year, my office has held more than 100 meetings and conversations with farmers, businesses, municipalities, ports and other stakeholders across Northwest Washington. I heard a consistent message: a stable economic relationship with Canada and Mexico is critical to keeping local businesses afloat, lowering costs, and creating good-paying jobs. Our region's farmers, manufacturers, ports, and other businesses depend on being able to trade reliably across the border. When trade policy changes abruptly and negotiations break down, that uncertainty has real consequences for workers and businesses here at home. Third, this could make a trade agreement that has worked for Northwest Washington less effective. For years, the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, known as USMCA, provided a framework for trade among the three countries. Many goods that were protected from import taxes under that agreement are now subject to these new tariffs. In July, I sent a report to the U.S. Trade Representative outlining what I heard from people across Northwest Washington and urging the continuation of USMCA. I have also worked with my colleagues on the New Democrat Coalition Trade and Tariffs Task Force to call for the agreement to be renewed and strengthened. There is still disagreement over why the latest negotiations between the United States and Canada broke down. But there should be no disagreement about the importance of getting our economic relationship back on stable ground. Canada is our neighbor, our ally, and one of our most important trading partners. As the top Democrat on the U.S.-Canada Interparliamentary Group, I have seen firsthand how much both countries benefit when we work together to solve shared challenges. The bottom line is simple: trade can create jobs and lower costs. Reckless tariffs can do the opposite. I will keep working to end these tariffs, bring down costs for families and businesses, and restore a stable economic relationship with Canada. And, frankly, I would like to make the U.S.-Canada relationship boring again. I'm sure you've seen the videos and images of the disastrous flooding in Nepal by now. I spent 80 days in Tibet, near the Tibetan-Nepali border, while climbing the north ridge of Everest and Cho Oyu, where I proposed to my husband. I have given my adult life to these mountains, to being a voice for the glaciers, the ice, and the people who live there. It is one of the poorest places in the world with the warmest, kindest people in the world. Seeing the death and destruction from the flooding, with that wall of water coming down the Trishuli last week, it hurt my heart in a way that's hard to convey.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f4970eb9-e21d-4dad-8e00-3d09d3245270?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On August 26th, a chunk of ice and rock the size of a neighborhood let go off Langtang Lirung and fell into the river below it. It hit hard enough that seismometers in Germany picked it up. All that debris plugged the river like a thumb over a hose, and for a few minutes everything downstream got quiet. Then the plug blew out. The water came down the valley at 30 feet high and it took the villages, the bridges, the hydropower plants, and the border crossing with it. Some of the people who died were found 150 miles away in India.
Now, more than 1,000 people are confirmed dead with thousands missing, including 85 Americans. Most of them are still up there under the mud. It is a tragedy that's difficult to comprehend.
People will say it was a freak event, an act of God, that nobody could have seen it coming. Some of the first reports said an earthquake caused it, and you will see people repeat that. But the [USGS looked at the seismic data ](https://substack.com/redirect/1f979bc6-0425-43d5-94a4-54354bcf6d5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and said the signal was caused by the landslide itself, not by an earthquake. The collapse was so big it registered as a magnitude 5.2 all on its own. There was no earthquake. There was just a mountain coming apart.
And this is the second time this exact river has flooded like this in fourteen months. Last time, nine people died. As climate change heats our planet, with the Himalayas warming at twice the global average, there are hundreds of glacial lakes hanging above villages that threaten millions of people downstream. Researchers have officially identified 47 potentially dangerous lakes, but the real number is much higher. Research from China's second Qinghai-Tibet scientific expedition, published in 2025, identified 1,256 high-risk glacial lakes. Of these, [182 were classified ](https://substack.com/redirect/b1578e29-904e-4f10-a5bd-0fe94092dfe5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as posing an extremely high risk of outburst flooding.
Almost none of these lakes have any kind of alarm on them. And we can put alarms on them, like the system that helped save hundreds of lives in Blatten, Switzerland. It's like a smoke detector for a mountain. There are sensors and satellites and sirens in a village. Nobody wakes up excited to hear their smoke detector going off. You put batteries in it and you don't think about it for years. It costs a few dollars to keep a battery in, and then one night it screams and you and your family get out of the house alive. You pay almost nothing for years so that you get eleven minutes of warning on that one night out of hundreds.
So why weren't smoke detectors installed in Nepal, and who took the batteries out?

In 2025 the Trump administration's DODGE efforts, led by Elon Musk,[ canceled $329 million in aid to Nepal](https://substack.com/redirect/26fd27c4-5e6e-4b14-bf41-4703438841d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You can read the list of what got killed. One of the lines on it is "support the government's disaster risk reduction efforts." Another one is about understanding earthquake and landslide hazard in Nepal. Those are the smoke detectors. We yanked them off the wall and threw them in a dumpster, and we did it in a country that sits directly downhill from the largest pile of melting ice on the planet.
In the initial response to the flood, the US government sent [$500,000](https://substack.com/redirect/a0c7db13-f1f3-412b-bebf-bf0bca8234aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for a disaster that erased entire towns and left almost one hundred Americans missing. That is less than Trump spent on a pedestal. This June, [Mother Jones ](https://substack.com/redirect/3ceb4e1d-1c16-4401-8e64-d50164b3b6c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)obtained contracting documents showing the National Park Service paid $527,226, in a no-bid contract, just to build the base for a statue of Caesar Rodney, a man who enslaved nearly two hundred people. They put it in Freedom Plaza, which was renamed in 1988 to honor Martin Luther King Jr.
The US has now pledged more than $3.5 million in humanitarian aid. But it is still pennies on the dollar compared to what we are spending on the Iran war. The Pentagon told senators in a closed-door briefing that the first six days of the Iran war cost at least[ $11.3 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/0267ab52-307d-4675-acbf-572b87dee8f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's about $1.9 billion a day, or $78 million an hour. Our entire humanitarian response to Nepal is less than three minutes of that war.
I acknowledge that many Americans are struggling to afford groceries and gas, and that funding for Nepal isn't a high priority. I hear the "America first" rhetoric. I get it. We can't solve every problem in the world. But we have a choice of what our taxpayer dollars support. Funding programs like USAID and disaster relief after catastrophic flooding, accelerated by climate change, is what we should prioritize. It's soft power. It shows the world we're good global citizens and neighbors, and it builds goodwill toward Americans. As the wealthiest country in the world, we could do so much to help Americans and others if we didn't spend so much on war and on hurting people. ICE alone received roughly [$75 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/464789c7-5219-4909-a862-f98adbd66126?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the last reconciliation bill alone, and it is being used to forcibly arrest and detain people without due process, many of whom are lawful immigrants or US citizens. Our national debt is now approaching $40 trillion. I get that we can't spend on everything. But Nepal is a drop in the bucket. I don't think that should be controversial.
Before I get into my other argument about why we should fund disaster relief for Nepal, and for FEMA here at home, I want to talk about why the ice is coming apart in the Himalayas in the first place.
Ice is what holds the big mountains together, in the Himalayas and the Alps and the Andes and Alaska and a lot of other places. It's like mortar in a wall. It fills the cracks in the rock and freezes them shut. When it stays frozen, the whole mountain stays in place for ten thousand years and looks permanent. But when you warm it up a couple of degrees, the mortar softens, the cracks open, and one day a piece of the wall the size of a town falls off. That's what we've known was going to happen for a long time.
Exxon, the oil and gas company, knew it first. Their own scientists ran the projections back in the 1970s and 80s. In 2023, researchers published a study in the journal Science where they went back and looked at those projections to see how accurate they were. Exxon's scientists were right. [Between 63 and 83 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/51deecc3-f5ce-4508-83d9-3545d2218ad4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of their projections matched reality.
After they ran those initial projections, they spent the [next thirty years and an enormous amount of money](https://substack.com/redirect/ae723b24-7dad-4731-8832-7de469a22e4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) telling the public that the science was unsettled, that the models were shaky, and that nobody really knew.
It's like reading an avalanche forecast. As a professional athlete, avalanches are one of the greatest risks I face, so I spend every morning in the winter reading avalanche forecasts to understand what the forecaster is seeing and to decide where to put my body in the mountains. That relationship only works because I trust that the person writing it is telling me the truth about what is buried in the snowpack. If I ever found out that a forecaster looked at a loaded slope, understood perfectly well that it was going to slide, and then wrote that conditions were stable because somebody paid him to write that, I would not call that a lie. It could kill me. It's deception. It should be criminal.
Exxon was the forecaster. They read the snowpack. They knew the slope was going to go. They told the whole world it was safe to ski it, and they kept profiting the entire time.
So when people ask whose fault this is, it is every executive who signed off on the deception, delay, and distortion campaigns. It's every consultant who got rich writing talking points that muddied the water and confused the public. It's every politician who took checks from fossil fuel companies and stood up and repeated those lies. They bought denial and delay, and the invoice came due in a valley in Nepal.
I know someone is going to point out that I flew to Tibet to climb those mountains, and that I've burned plenty of carbon getting to the places I love. That's true. It's also exactly why I don't accept that this is a story about individual choices. The people who spent thirty years lying about this would love for us to spend the next thirty arguing about each other's flights. I'm not doing that. I want the people who profited from the lie to pay for the damage. Exxon should pay to help rebuild this part of Nepal [(they made $160 million per day last quarter as oil prices have surged). ](https://substack.com/redirect/90953b04-d1c8-4aaf-a5ed-f272141bea85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The United States has put the vast majority of climate-warming emissions into the atmosphere to build the wealth we have. The people of Nepal have used the smallest amount of fossil fuels. They did not profit from it. They just happened to be standing underneath. The people getting hit the hardest contributed the least.
So please contribute to Nepal and Tibet relief today. I trust the [Nepal Red Cross ](https://substack.com/redirect/79ddec3a-82fe-4d4e-8434-48150cf1f77e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Society and the [American Himalayan Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/6e5a09a0-9312-4daf-9d4d-ccda5443d260?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), all of which work directly with communities in these districts and have been on the ground there for years. Then [contact your senators and representatives](https://substack.com/redirect/e8e32f36-e11a-4314-8b52-7eb01b36006a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and tell them to restore the disaster aid and USAID funding we cut, because a siren in the mountains is cheaper than a funeral and a rescue operation in a remote Himalayan village. And stop letting anyone in a suit tell you that the companies who lied about this for thirty years should not have to pay for the damage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3f59c2f2-f9a8-4abe-b2b5-537eed1e1443?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

---|---|---
In other news, [Patagonia sued the Trump administration](https://substack.com/redirect/30e8b278-c6ce-494d-9a0d-e24975bdff08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over the National monuments. I went down there last week to explore Trump's shrinkage, to visit the parts of the monument that were cut with my friend [Len Necefer](https://open.substack.com/users/36345321-len-necefer?utm_source=mentions). More to come on that. Then, I had the opportunity to join professional skipper Francesca Clapcich on a 60-foot racing sailboat that's currently racing to France from New York City. That's about $1.9 billion a day, or $78 million an hour. Our entire humanitarian response to Nepal is less than three minutes of that war. I acknowledge that many Americans are struggling to afford groceries and gas, and that funding for Nepal isn't a high priority. I hear the "America first" rhetoric. I get it. We can't solve every problem in the world. But we have a choice of what our taxpayer dollars support. Funding programs like USAID and disaster relief after catastrophic flooding, accelerated by climate change, is what we should prioritize. It's soft power. It shows the world we're good global citizens and neighbors, and it builds goodwill toward Americans. As the wealthiest country in the world, we could do so much to help Americans and others if we didn't spend so much on war and on hurting people. ICE alone received roughly in the last reconciliation bill alone, and it is being used to forcibly arrest and detain people without due process, many of whom are lawful immigrants or US citizens. Our national debt is now approaching $40 trillion. I get that we can't spend on everything. But Nepal is a drop in the bucket. I don't think that should be controversial. Before I get into my other argument about why we should fund disaster relief for Nepal, and for FEMA here at home, I want to talk about why the ice is coming apart in the Himalayas in the first place. Ice is what holds the big mountains together, in the Himalayas and the Alps and the Andes and Alaska and a lot of other places. It's like mortar in a wall. It fills the cracks in the rock and freezes them shut. When it stays frozen, the whole mountain stays in place for ten thousand years and looks permanent. But when you warm it up a couple of degrees, the mortar softens, the cracks open, and one day a piece of the wall the size of a town falls off. That's what we've known was going to happen for a long time. Exxon, the oil and gas company, knew it first. Their own scientists ran the projections back in the 1970s and 80s. In 2023, researchers published a study in the journal Science where they went back and looked at those projections to see how accurate they were. Exxon's scientists were right. of their projections matched reality. After they ran those initial projections, they spent the telling the public that the science was unsettled, that the models were shaky, and that nobody really knew. It's like reading an avalanche forecast. As a professional athlete, avalanches are one of the greatest risks I face, so I spend every morning in the winter reading avalanche forecasts to understand what the forecaster is seeing and to decide where to put my body in the mountains. That relationship only works because I trust that the person writing it is telling me the truth about what is buried in the snowpack. If I ever found out that a forecaster looked at a loaded slope, understood perfectly well that it was going to slide, and then wrote that conditions were stable because somebody paid him to write that, I would not call that a lie. It could kill me. It's deception. It should be criminal. Exxon was the forecaster. They read the snowpack. They knew the slope was going to go. They told the whole world it was safe to ski it, and they kept profiting the entire time. So when people ask whose fault this is, it is every executive who signed off on the deception, delay, and distortion campaigns. It's every consultant who got rich writing talking points that muddied the water and confused the public. It's every politician who took checks from fossil fuel companies and stood up and repeated those lies. They bought denial and delay, and the invoice came due in a valley in Nepal. I know someone is going to point out that I flew to Tibet to climb those mountains, and that I've burned plenty of carbon getting to the places I love. That's true. It's also exactly why I don't accept that this is a story about individual choices. The people who spent thirty years lying about this would love for us to spend the next thirty arguing about each other's flights. I'm not doing that. I want the people who profited from the lie to pay for the damage. Exxon should pay to help rebuild this part of Nepal The United States has put the vast majority of climate-warming emissions into the atmosphere to build the wealth we have. The people of Nepal have used the smallest amount of fossil fuels. They did not profit from it. They just happened to be standing underneath. The people getting hit the hardest contributed the least. So please contribute to Nepal and Tibet relief today. I trust the and the , all of which work directly with communities in these districts and have been on the ground there for years. Then and tell them to restore the disaster aid and USAID funding we cut, because a siren in the mountains is cheaper than a funeral and a rescue operation in a remote Himalayan village. And stop letting anyone in a suit tell you that the companies who lied about this for thirty years should not have to pay for the damage. | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- In other news, over the National monuments. I went down there last week to explore Trump's shrinkage, to visit the parts of the monument that were cut with my friend . More to come on that. Then, I had the opportunity to join professional skipper Francesca Clapcich on a 60-foot racing sailboat that's currently racing to France from New York City. subject: RE: Philadelphia cannot keep dumping its pollution on Black communities
body:
Reworld wants years more of Philadelphia’s trash. The City Council can stop it. | |
---
Peter, **Reworld waste management wants the Philadelphia City Council to approve another long-term contract that would keep Philadelphia trash flowing to the company’s incinerator in Chester.** Reworld has spent big to protect a profitable arrangement. Its previous Philadelphia contract was worth tens of millions of dollars, and the company spent more than $100,000 lobbying the City Council and the Parker administration while the city considered its next waste contracts. Chester has been left carrying the cost. The majority-Black city has spent decades living with pollution from a massive incinerator that burns trash hauled in from Philadelphia and across the region. **Corporate money can buy lobbyists and access. But it cannot match what happens when people organize together, raise our voices, and make elected officials answer publicly for whose interests they serve.** [**Tell the Philadelphia City Council to reject the Reworld contract and stop sending Philadelphia’s trash to be burned in Chester.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_-6ezreVUDKM4uYMpG61B3tmZL107ueVKGrZcnb23wpIlNenMRc0EGDKYwCt9bDYoMDJMpGhP2LgFfCXKiSKRlKIdB9gTMnvhuAd1inXxcj4LeoEUydL_3jiA08U5wp75n-vymsuswbb1tjivW69wzx7aAw8xqwGbvrZsMyZcA4HwERVDtkLDQsQ-rmqhfiogmblG5Z1yeGX8yFH125RcxInu5K26q8nwxTRsS-hxG5z9WOZFzeEkxxZBV03rlGybLfZNfcHagxjqZaUGKSahSZe6shiwLxAQeX-tWxe3ww3juulbsJnbUAPu9tWsrLsc7IXzJE03UwKtmbkplhjEgkm9MqXsucjjjicxNz_fuN1pY8ejRK5Ovj4WwlNG_rzU/4tp/H-_f6yadQYWvSnzjxni0tA/h0/h001.MC0jEDMazRmWgNsm3nBkdDXgDTGPCfCmFXhYztBe3zA) | | [DEMAND ACTION](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_-6ezreVUDKM4uYMpG61B3tmZL107ueVKGrZcnb23wpLYdlLiQkASml6ohag1a_ds9UMAowi3DTV9ZnevzaPeqhMbbABW37K1tZsOs3uZDUPTjceZhPAQYq1iwuSB8mZSOn3YdAIkowiQJ9FSvS1C4LKb8b1FH4WNT4Y2AGFvZSXVPbZOBB_OKYDHVDNHmZIYFHTYrMO_-W2nPzPnBR30HPke_pl0oMhdiC9W_bBnsI7B9-4japuqf1IbBo0LQZt3AaTfSKGb-jP1vaTf96CJyX5m7YK09UZaNKK9It2bv9wv0OZleuxCwNOG1strxlgd8OT68S5xbNR-lKCqNpt4LAhsCjUZ4Ep5SVFmt08uvKl44czyHslJl6i7EsZk722c/4tp/H-_f6yadQYWvSnzjxni0tA/h1/h001.8FFgddn8T2qQny1yXcqjQJbBiBsG-NUbGG5kVszouiY)

**Nearly 40% of Philadelphia’s trash was burned under its previous waste contracts, most of it at Reworld’s Chester facility. Another contract could keep that relationship going for as many as 7 more years.**
That means this vote is about much more than where garbage goes after it leaves the curb. It is about whether Black communities will keep being expected to absorb pollution created by decisions made somewhere else.
Workers at the facility deserve economic security too. Corporate executives should never be allowed to pit good jobs against healthy communities and use workers as a shield for maintaining a profitable arrangement. Philadelphia has the resources and responsibility to demand better.
**Chester residents have organized for years because lasting change has never come from waiting for powerful institutions to do the right thing on their own. It comes when communities build enough collective power to demand it.**
[**Take action now and tell the Philadelphia City Council that Chester cannot remain a sacrifice zone for Philadelphia’s trash.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_-6ezreVUDKM4uYMpG61B3tmZL107ueVKGrZcnb23wpEckMsAYG5SoT82SMnV1aJ5PeWfejzAyreeCs6fzhufrQOCaAZcPcrEycTcHhAZyrJfVgnYaYQHtydOJmOHxAcgoo8wK4t-r2vBq7624bhaTuyDNAnblavQqBhN2m712qpy5KbjCwEvF6EusEzEcw5Mr2G8ZeOMIjUDi6Ofuar0kkdgi7DnnrDVAJHbYgx4Gz0mqIU8DDEKQ7PMbpyQCBR7iSSKWjZ2dqjxc36T5CHqVZ-VpjbHLpsaYL1AYh3wVO_fZZr5h8U-4Zi7BwLd31hGmhCAmQv4ffUBTCyaMIQK6xcqb3TjDX0AhlT_-GqZElwO9jdoR1lvs6bBS08KWbAQ/4tp/H-_f6yadQYWvSnzjxni0tA/h2/h001.S0eX-0Hz7FGsJzXt3CabBbNtF-gQPAGOSOdd31Nvcik)

clean_body: Reworld wants years more of Philadelphia’s trash. The City Council can stop it. | | Peter, Reworld waste management wants the Philadelphia City Council to approve another long-term contract that would keep Philadelphia trash flowing to the company’s incinerator in Chester. Reworld has spent big to protect a profitable arrangement. Its previous Philadelphia contract was worth tens of millions of dollars, and the company spent more than $100,000 lobbying the City Council and the Parker administration while the city considered its next waste contracts. Chester has been left carrying the cost. The majority-Black city has spent decades living with pollution from a massive incinerator that burns trash hauled in from Philadelphia and across the region. Corporate money can buy lobbyists and access. But it cannot match what happens when people organize together, raise our voices, and make elected officials answer publicly for whose interests they serve. | | Nearly 40% of Philadelphia’s trash was burned under its previous waste contracts, most of it at Reworld’s Chester facility. Another contract could keep that relationship going for as many as 7 more years. That means this vote is about much more than where garbage goes after it leaves the curb. It is about whether Black communities will keep being expected to absorb pollution created by decisions made somewhere else. Workers at the facility deserve economic security too. Corporate executives should never be allowed to pit good jobs against healthy communities and use workers as a shield for maintaining a profitable arrangement. Philadelphia has the resources and responsibility to demand better. Chester residents have organized for years because lasting change has never come from waiting for powerful institutions to do the right thing on their own. It comes when communities build enough collective power to demand it. | | Friends,

After a decade of hard work, we have achieved an enormous victory!

**I was proud to recently announce that the site of a proposed asphalt plant along the Cedar River has been officially purchased by King County. The land will now be preserved for public use.**

This was a long and difficult fight, but we've stood together since the beginning. And in the midst of all the protests, letters, and moratoriums, I was drafting legislation to purchase and preserve land along this corridor. Now, five years after I first drafted that legislation, we were able to make it happen.
**[READ THE KOMO NEWS STORY HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/maHAUrEa9u2?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)** [](https://us.list-manage.com/PnQZInm3TzF?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166) **_" This is a fight we as a community have been waging for nearly a decade to protect our river, our natural habitats, and our community. Today, that fight has finally come to an end, and we can shift our focus from stopping what shouldn't be to building what should -- parks, open spaces, and a place the public can enjoy for generations."
\- Councilmember Reagan Dunn_**
**\------------------------
[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/9XFWIrrTh_5?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)
\------------------------**
**This is what fighting for our community looks like.** It took creativity, collaboration, negotiation, and a lot of time and sweat, but, like all of you, I would do it all over again if I had to.

Wins like this demonstrate why we can never give up -- _future generations are relying on us_.

**But I need your help. Would you consider**[**making a contribution of $35, $50, $75 or more**](https://us.list-manage.com/n0kOa1oFy2s?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)** to help me continue protecting our neighborhoods, open spaces, and public resources?**
With [your help](https://us.list-manage.com/1Chy9d5wm7Q?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166), I won't stop securing wins for our community!

Thank you for your support! Reagan Dunn

body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260902-2666-foote&t=1001&akid=2666%2E342411%2EOjVAl6 ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter, we didn’t
want to have to send this email.

We set a goal for last month: raise $125,000 to fuel this movement through
the final stretch of the cycle. We missed it, which puts us behind right
when we can't afford to be.

Our Squad — Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida — have all won their
primaries and are officially moving on to November.

They got here by refusing to back down — from corporate PACs, from Trump's
authoritarianism, from anyone who told them and their communities to wait
their turn. They've spent this campaign on the ground, building the kind
of grassroots power that can't be bought.

Now they're heading into a general election where the same outside forces
and Trump’s MAGA machine will spend whatever it takes to unseat them and
silence this movement.

But we have something that can't be bought: this grassroots movement —
people chipping in what they can, when they can, because they believe in
something bigger than themselves.

We've won before with grassroots power, and we can do it again. But it
only works if we show up when it counts, and right now, we're short.
That's why we're reaching out.

name: Wes Moore
subject: "Thank God we're in Maryland"
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1863%2E1086043%2EBQJPwQ)
Hey Peter, it’s Wes. **_Thank God We’re in Maryland._**
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260902-2.TiIvba&refcode=em-20260902-2&t=2&akid=1863%2E1086043%2EBQJPwQ)
That’s more than just one of my favorite shirts. ☝🏽 It’s how I feel when I look at everything we’ve accomplished together.
We've seen the greatest public safety turnaround in the country. We've put $100 million back in people's pockets through utility relief. And we've given young Marylanders a first-of-its-kind service year option, creating a pathway to build their futures.
**That’s what governing for the people looks like.[To keep me in that fight for another term, will you chip in to our re-election campaign today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260902-2.TiIvba&refcode=em-20260902-2&t=3&akid=1863%2E1086043%2EBQJPwQ)**
When I look at what's happening in Washington — I'm even more grateful for our team here in Maryland.
Dan Cox and MAGA Republicans want to take back the governor's office and roll back every bit of this progress. They’re against everything we’ve built together. **_We can't let that happen._**
**[Can you chip in $10 to help us keep our opponents from rolling back our progress?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260902-2.TiIvba&refcode=em-20260902-2&t=4&akid=1863%2E1086043%2EBQJPwQ)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260902-2.TiIvba&amount=5&refcode=em-20260902-2&t=23&akid=1863%2E1086043%2EBQJPwQ)**
So yeah – Thank God we're in Maryland.
— Wes Moore

subject: 🌵 This Week in LD2: Community, Leadership & New Endorsements
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTE BOLICK
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/eKwZMofUwn3?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
| | | | | | 📅 **September 2nd Update** 🌆 Community Leadership & EngagementLast week, I joined local community leaders for an evening brainstorming session with First Place Global, where we explored innovative ideas to support neurodiverse adults and strengthen independent‐living pathways. The conversations were thoughtful, creative, and deeply rooted in community need.I also had the privilege of visiting a constituent in her assisted‐living center. She is seeking support for an emotional‐support animal trained to detect her oncoming seizures. I assured her I would help research nonprofits that work in this space — ensuring she has access to the resources she needs.Tomorrow morning, I’ll meet with local leaders and the Arouet Foundation to continue discussions on workforce development, second‐chance opportunities, and community reintegration.
🎙 Education & Youth OutreachI was recently invited by Liberty International to narrate an upcoming educational animated project introducing middle school students to the philosophical ideas in Ayn Rand’s Anthem. They had seen one of my campaign videos, liked my voice, and asked me to lend it to their national project. I’m honored to support efforts that encourage critical thinking and civic literacy among young learners.
🏘 Housing & AffordabilityAffordability remains one of the top issues among general election voters. Last week, I met with a representative from Pew Charitable Trusts while they were in Phoenix for a statewide housing conference. It was an excellent opportunity to learn more about their research, discuss Arizona’s unique challenges, and share ideas for next steps as we prepare for the upcoming legislative session.
🏛 Political & Community EngagementAs a legislator serving in one of Arizona’s most competitive districts, I attended the joint House and Senate Victory Fund reception to thank the many donors and supporters working to help us maintain a majority at the Capitol. Their commitment to civic engagement and public service is invaluable.My husband and I also spoke at the Workplace Integrity Institute’s lunch‐and‐learn event. We were surrounded by exceptional leaders from the business community, nonprofit sector, courts, and government. Sharing our experiences on integrity in the workplace was an honor, and the conversations among attendees were both compelling and inspiring.🔔 New Campaign Endorsements
* Paul Johnson, Chairman of No Labels and a registered LD2 voter, shared this powerful endorsement:

“Shawnna Bolick has grit. She reminds me of the Arizona leaders of the past — people who had the backbone to fight for our community when conscience and conviction demanded it.Shawnna is committed to working with both parties to find solutions... On behalf of the Arizona Independent Party and our thousands of members, we are proud to endorse Shawnna Bolick for State Senate.”I’m honored to have earned the endorsement of the [No Labels Party / Arizona Independent Party](https://us.list-manage.com/myNDHFm2xgD?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) and look forward to continuing our work on common‐sense solutions when I am re‐elected this November.
* Americans for Prosperity (AFP) Arizona Action Endorsement

Stephen Shadegg, Senior Advisor to AFP Action, issued the following [statement](https://us.list-manage.com/dRSDTPE1e9E?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211):“Arizona families are paying more for groceries, housing, and electricity than they were two years ago... The candidates we are endorsing have shown us they will hold the line on spending, keep Arizona’s tax code competitive, and protect the school choice programs tens of thousands of families depend on.”I’m grateful for AFP Action’s support and their commitment to engaging voters directly in the neighborhoods where the future of our legislature will be decided.♿ Disability Rights ArizonaI also participated in a Disability Rights Arizona advocacy event, continuing my long‐standing commitment to ensuring vulnerable Arizonans have access to the services, protections, and support they deserve.📰 Campaign Call to ActionThe outcome of the election of my race will determine the composition of the State Senate. Once again, we are in the national spotlight. I represent the most highly competitive State Senate district in Arizona, and your support can make a meaningful difference. If you live in District 2 and would like to request a yard sign, we would be happy to deliver one to you. Please [email me](https://us.list-manage.com/6PEln2cwShG?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) and we will make it happen!If you’re interested in helping to volunteer assemble campaign post cards, please [email me](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=Volunteer&body=) so we can get it scheduled. 📆 **Upcoming Fundraiser** 📍 September 16, 2026Fundraiser – North Scottsdale🕠 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM📩 [RSVP for the address](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I%20want%20to%20help%20Shawnna%20on%209%2F16&body=).
If you can’t attend, but you’d like to make a donation, you can make a secure donation [online](https://us.list-manage.com/aekvX2BzY5O?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) today. I appreciate your continued support and for staying informed as we move into the heart of the 2026 election cycle. LD 2 is a competitive, but balanced legislative district.
Thank you for your continued support!Best,Shawnna

name: Rashida Tlaib
subject: Help progressives win this November:
body:
With primaries nearly done, we’re gearing up for November’s elections. | | |
---
Friend, Our movement is building momentum, with progressive candidates winning across the country — including U.S. Senate candidate Ed Markey, who resoundingly defeated a moderate Democrat last night in Massachusetts. Primary election season is nearly done, but the fight isn’t over: We’re gearing up for this November’s general election. **We need a strong grassroots effort starting**** _now_****to win in November** and make people's lives better. **One of the progressive candidates I’m proud to support is my friend Tiffany Tilley, a champion for social justice** who’s running for re-election to Michigan’s State Board of Education. name: Ruben Gallego
subject: A pretty crazy story, if you have a minute
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Hola, Peter. It’s Ruben.
You might be wondering how this kid...
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=1&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
...ended up here, on TV with Stephen Colbert, serving in the U.S. Senate, and squaring off against the worst president in American history.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=2&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
Well, it started back in the apartment I shared with my mom and my sisters. It was tough. I was sleeping on the floor because that’s all we could afford.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=3&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
I knew I had to do whatever it took to build a better life for us. I worked a bunch of jobs all through school to help make ends meet. Thanks to my family, my community, and a lot of hard work, I got into Harvard. But before I graduated, I enlisted in the Marines to serve the country that gave me so much.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=4&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
I deployed to al Anbar, Iraq with my brothers in arms. We ended up the hardest hit Marine unit of the entire Iraq war, and I lost some of my best friends over there. After we came home I knew I had to do something to improve things for the guys I served with, for people who grew up like me. So, I ended up running for Congress — and I won.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=5&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
Then, on January 6th, everything changed. It became clear to me that public service wasn’t just about improving the lives of the people in my community anymore — it was about defending our democracy, too.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=6&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
So, I ran for Senate against one of Trump’s most loyal foot soldiers. And thanks to the support of millions of people, my friends, and my family, I won. Now, it’s my job to square off against Trump every day to defend our people and our Constitution.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=7&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)
When I was a Marine in Iraq, I never would’ve thought I’d have to fight to defend our democracy at home.
And honestly, I never, ever would’ve thought I’d need to ask supporters like you, people who have already done so much, to do a bit more. But to keep up the fight and lead the nationwide grassroots mobilization we’ll need to combat everything Trump’s doing, that’s what I have to do.
[**Please — if you can afford to make a donation of $5 or anything you can it would mean the world to me. We’re coming up on our official FEC deadline this month, and we can’t miss our goals.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-aug26.NoGKRq&refcode=em260902-1-160&t=8&akid=4199%2E734936%2EMNG6i1)

Thanks to my family, my community, and a lot of hard work, I got into Harvard. But before I graduated, I enlisted in the Marines to serve the country that gave me so much. I deployed to al Anbar, Iraq with my brothers in arms. We ended up the hardest hit Marine unit of the entire Iraq war, and I lost some of my best friends over there. After we came home I knew I had to do something to improve things for the guys I served with, for people who grew up like me. So, I ended up running for Congress — and I won. Then, on January 6th, everything changed. It became clear to me that public service wasn’t just about improving the lives of the people in my community anymore — it was about defending our democracy, too. So, I ran for Senate against one of Trump’s most loyal foot soldiers. And thanks to the support of millions of people, my friends, and my family, I won. Now, it’s my job to square off against Trump every day to defend our people and our Constitution. When I was a Marine in Iraq, I never would’ve thought I’d have to fight to defend our democracy at home. And honestly, I never, ever would’ve thought I’d need to ask supporters like you, people who have already done so much, to do a bit more. But to keep up the fight and lead the nationwide grassroots mobilization we’ll need to combat everything Trump’s doing, that’s what I have to do. If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly. | | ** | | | | | | | ** Thank you. I couldn’t do this without you and the team we’ve built together. Semper Fi, Ruben Paid For By Gallego for Arizona Use of military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform do not imply endorsement by the Department of the Navy or the Department of Defense.

**At a young age, I joined the United States Marine Corps to defend our country and ultimately earned the rank of Sergeant before my discharge.** Once I entered civilian life, I started my entrepreneurial career owning a successful small computer business until my son took over the family business.

I’ve seen firsthand how today’s Democratic Party has abandoned working families. Every single day, I hear from constituents who are struggling with everyday challenges. **In short, my son, Nicholas, was tragically stabbed to death and murdered in 2016.**

If you’re a parent, I’m sure you could imagine how devastating this was for me. Nicholas was only 28 at the time and did not deserve what happened.

He had followed in my footsteps and joined the Marine Corps. He was a father to two children – my grandchildren. When it happened, no one came forward with any information, and the case to find the killer went cold.

**I decided to take a stand, to fight for the rule of law and public safety so that no other family has to experience the same tragedy.** Five years later, I ran for City Council in Hemet. I won, and just a few months later, our amazing law enforcement found the killer and arrested him.

**As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration.** America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY.

**Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration.** Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security.

**On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement.** After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness.

**As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around.** Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. I’ll do everything in my power as a Congressman to support our military so we prioritize READINESS over WOKENESS.

**Finally, we must dismantle DEI in every corner of the government.** DOGE’s work to cut wasteful spending has been a great start, but we must continue to fight to lower the cost of living, defend free speech, and usher in the Golden Age of America.

**WHY DO I NEED YOUR HELP?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=fc6b54318d424cf293933f821764bd71&_e=d763Ia91vE6579UN-ya2T8w33HBN-xXlFakRw3v_l6mrJtMuJK_5ND_qWCBEapDFVTa7cAN3UaXNGT_FZaX42EGt7YJ79WcG6I7m1cageytct6sMfL-5U4jN0JzF5GZ7fl45-5Qq_3dOU1bpm7kn5tbHOZluVdmygCtszcu_dGztHF57OxNWLMM9aEb0bYSlrdYKi2978p3SRGqbTaFeKqN1wJykINiQ2Q4-sDheup3EPGv4Rj2QO4zHjtbCfuXKpZmvKT-FmVh0VdRKyjL4DVo_vU9bvS4P9-hTY_9JsqSwbxFlz6QRmz1UP0GD38O_7u2SB4ZOnDoSocfiXoomlD-coFhMU0FfHpgNu-rmolQyBFaGL4CTUw1cNYErBUNWgVF3uGJG-SZ7VDt0dCx4lqzpmAXNaIq19nKibnpm-e6GOdeSLC0iWgIF6QzbvvXRxrs6tc45axTUmL71bNIC45sB54ekUCbJGkOb7KFee2MM4STIgi9IKdmnZ9-39-pe64fJpvkwDHn_Y4tV9i4umw%3D%3D)

**Simply put – the Radical Left has a stranglehold on California.** Just like they’re trying to flip Texas Blue, I’m trying to flip California Red. It may seem impossible, but so many Californians are sick and tired of suffering under Gavin Newsom, Nancy Pelosi, and Adam Schiff’s leadership here. I know many people who have left California just because of the politicians who want to turn our beautiful state into a Communist Utopia.

Together, we can fight and WIN._
