Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Now, they stand for DEI, wokeness, putting Americans last, and doing everything they can to fight against President Trump. As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration. America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY. Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration. Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security. On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement. After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness. As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around. Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. I’ll do everything in my power as a Congressman to support our military so we prioritize READINESS over WOKENESS. Finally, we must dismantle DEI in every corner of the government. DOGE’s work to cut wasteful spending has been a great start, but we must continue to fight to lower the cost of living, defend free speech, and usher in the Golden Age of America. WHY DO I NEED YOUR HELP? Simply put – the Radical Left has a stranglehold on California. Just like they’re trying to flip Texas Blue, I’m trying to flip California Red. It may seem impossible, but so many Californians are sick and tired of suffering under Gavin Newsom, Nancy Pelosi, and Adam Schiff’s leadership here. I know many people who have left California just because of the politicians who want to turn our beautiful state into a Communist Utopia. But Newsom, Pelosi, and Schiff have MILLIONS of dollars in reserve, ready to spend against my campaign to prevent common sense leadership. They only care about lining their own pockets, even if their constituents suffer. It’s going to be an uphill battle, but if there’s one thing I learned as a Marine, it’s that the only way to create a better tomorrow is through dedicated hard work and grit. Together, we can fight and WIN. | Thank you for taking the time to read all of this. I truly appreciate it. Semper Fidelis, Joe Males Meet Joe Males: Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission. Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved. Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same. Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy. During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: I tell this story not because it is special, but because of how common it is.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
I grew up in a working-class family.
My mom cleaned houses and my dad worked to build a small business. They worked themselves to the bone so that my brother and I could have a shot at making it.
And for a moment there, it looked like everything was on track: we had a home, bills were a little less stressful to pay, and I was doing well in school. What may have looked like a modest life to others was a dream come true for us.
But out of nowhere, when I was a teenager, my dad was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer. He passed away in September of 2008, just as the economy crashed thanks to the greed of Wall Street and millions of jobs across this country vanished.
It felt like the world of our family fell apart as the larger world was falling apart, too.
Overnight, my mom was left to figure out how to provide for two kids by herself, keep our house, pay off my dad's medical bills — all on a house cleaner's salary.
**I tell this story not because it is special, but because of how common it is.**
While the details may differ, so many of us know what it feels like to be one bad day, one piece of bad news, one small setback from everything falling apart.
**But we don't have to live like this in the richest country on earth.**
We can build a new world, a better future, where we guarantee the dignity of all of our people.
That future looks like **living wages.**
It looks like **stable housing.**
It looks like **Medicare for All.**
And it looks like **respect for all of our differences** , no matter who we are or where we come from.
Right now, we must out-organize the oligarchy and we cannot beat them if we take their money.
That is why, even as a waitress with a long-shot campaign, I decided that **I would never take money from lobbyists or corporations — and I never will.**

In solidarity,
Alexandria

| | **✅ Kean Bill to Expand Veteran Mental Health Services ✅**
---
| | Recently, Congressman Kean introduced legislation to expand access to mental health counseling through Vet Centers for both veterans and their families nationwide. Vet Centers provide critical services, including mental health support, and ensuring veterans and their loved ones can access the care they need remains an important priority. _“Veterans sacrifice so much to keep our nation safe and deserve access to quality mental health care close to home. Many veterans in New Jersey and across the country are faced with long, sometimes impossible travel to get the help they need. I worked across the aisle to find a solution.”_** _-_ Congressman Tom Kean Jr.**

| | It was another action-packed week on the road! We kicked things off with a packed kickoff dinner to officially launch the Women for Kean Coalition, led by Co-Chairs Janice Fields, Rhonda Kean, Bonnie Schmidt, Amanda Ackerman, Cathy Callahan, Rachel Rodriguez, Sharyn Alban, and Nancy Nelson. We were incredibly grateful to have RNC Co-Chair K.C. Crosbie join us and headline the evening - what a fun night with women joining us from across NJ-07!

From there, Tom stopped by a packed door launch at Union County GOP Headquarters to rally volunteers before heading to Lima Family Farms in Hillsborough for Agriculture in Action Open House Week. He then made a stop at the Branchburg door launch before joining the community at the Food Truck & Music Festival. The week wrapped up in Tewksbury at the return of the Sundowner Event, where Tom enjoyed catching up with friends and members of the Tewksbury Republican Committee.

As we get closer to Election Day, we continue to have weekend door launches in all six counties and will start weekly phone banks in all counties this upcoming week. This past week, we have had door knocking teams in **Bernards Township, Branchburg, Bridgewater, Clinton Township, Hampton, Holland, Hopatcong, Long Hill, Lopatcong, Mount Olive, Mountainside, New Providence, Phillipsburg, Rahway, Washington Borough,** and **Westfield**.

clean_body: Updates from our week in the field| | | | | Friend, | | Happy Wednesday, Team Kean! We are heading into another big week and the countdown is officially on now that we are just two months away until Election Day. These next few weeks will fly by, so now is the time to get involved, stay engaged, and make sure every day counts. There’s plenty of work ahead, and we’re excited to have you along with us for the final stretch! | | | | | | | ✅ Kean Bill to Expand Veteran Mental Health Services ✅ | | Recently, Congressman Kean introduced legislation to expand access to mental health counseling through Vet Centers for both veterans and their families nationwide. Vet Centers provide critical services, including mental health support, and ensuring veterans and their loved ones can access the care they need remains an important priority. “Veterans sacrifice so much to keep our nation safe and deserve access to quality mental health care close to home. Many veterans in New Jersey and across the country are faced with long, sometimes impossible travel to get the help they need. I worked across the aisle to find a solution.” - Congressman Tom Kean Jr. | | | | | Field Update | | | | | | | | | | It was another action-packed week on the road! We kicked things off with a packed kickoff dinner to officially launch the Women for Kean Coalition, led by Co-Chairs Janice Fields, Rhonda Kean, Bonnie Schmidt, Amanda Ackerman, Cathy Callahan, Rachel Rodriguez, Sharyn Alban, and Nancy Nelson. We were incredibly grateful to have RNC Co-Chair K.C. Crosbie join us and headline the evening - what a fun night with women joining us from across NJ-07! From there, Tom stopped by a packed door launch at Union County GOP Headquarters to rally volunteers before heading to Lima Family Farms in Hillsborough for Agriculture in Action Open House Week. He then made a stop at the Branchburg door launch before joining the community at the Food Truck & Music Festival. The week wrapped up in Tewksbury at the return of the Sundowner Event, where Tom enjoyed catching up with friends and members of the Tewksbury Republican Committee. As we get closer to Election Day, we continue to have weekend door launches in all six counties and will start weekly phone banks in all counties this upcoming week. This past week, we have had door knocking teams in Bernards Township, Branchburg, Bridgewater, Clinton Township, Hampton, Holland, Hopatcong, Long Hill, Lopatcong, Mount Olive, Mountainside, New Providence, Phillipsburg, Rahway, Washington Borough, and Westfield. Want to come to a door launch or phone bank? Sign up below! | | | | | | | | | | | | 🚨 NEW AD ALERT 🚨 | | "Every Patient 30s | Tom Kean for Congress \(New Jersey's 7th District\") | "Proud 30s | Tom Kean for Congress \(New Jersey's 7th District\") | | Since the last weekly update, the Kean For Congress Team has released two different ads - check them out here! In “,” Tom talks about his record of standing up to big insurance companies and fighting to protect patients from denied care and excessive costs for lifesaving treatments. “,” which was released this morning, is narrated by Tom’s father, Gov. Kean, and highlights Tom’s work to protect Medicare and Medicaid for every New Jersey senior, child, disabled person. * * *
I was sitting in the middle row, with Tyler Robinson directly in my view. He sat there completely still for nine hours straight. Didn't move a muscle.
The morning started slowly, with defense attorneys arguing that the public shouldn't be able to see the prosecution's witness, but suddenly we reached a decisive moment.
Tyler Robinson's text messages were on the screen, and I listened as the investigator read, "gramps' gun does just fine." They were reading messages from Tyler Robinson to his friends about how he murdered Charlie Kirk in cold blood.
I heard an outcry to my right. It was Erika.
Erika Kirk and Charlie's parents were weeping quietly after hearing Robinson's callous messages. We couldn't console them. The court didn't allow it. My job was to sit there and see the evidence.
As an Orem, Utah native, I attended the preliminary hearing two months ago.
This week, it came to a head.

_**(Piece continues)**_
After hearing from witnesses for five days straight, Tyler Robinson's team announced that they were requesting briefing and final arguments.
This meant two more months of written arguments, with the culminating day of final arguments from both sides taking place on September 1.
That day has come, and it went exactly as the prosecutors wanted.
After another brief stint of trying to keep the cameras out of the courtroom, unsuccessfully, I might add, the defense took their seats as the prosecution laid out their evidence once again.
They laid out the events of September 10: how Tyler Robinson left his home in Hurricane, Utah, very early in order to get to campus. He staked out UVU twice on camera, changed his clothes, and returned a third time. He ditched his car, raced to the top of the Losee rooftop, lay in wait, and shot Charlie Kirk. He then ran away, stashed the gun in a nearby bush, and left campus.
Later that night, he tried to recover his gun twice, failed both times, and returned home. A day later, he turned himself in to the police after being positively identified by his parents.
The defense did not dispute the evidence. Instead, they challenged counts 6 and 7 against him, which dealt with witness tampering and violence in the presence of a minor, and then rested.
After taking a one-hour break to deliberate, the judge returned and bound Tyler Robinson over for trial on all seven counts. In his own words the evidence was "substantial."

Instead, they challenged counts 6 and 7 against him, which dealt with witness tampering and violence in the presence of a minor, and then rested. After taking a one-hour break to deliberate, the judge returned and bound Tyler Robinson over for trial on all seven counts. In his own words the evidence was "substantial." We should bear in mind that while the trial will be a fantastic opportunity to get transparency and justice surrounding this case, it likely won't occur for months, if not years. Until then, the waiting game begins. But my job remains the same. I'll keep tracking the filings, I'll keep showing up to the courtroom, and I'll keep bringing the facts directly to you as they unfold. Charlie's family deserves that transparency, and I'll be here to see this through to the very end. | A guest post by| a political commentator, author, and conservative columnist. Now I need you to look at what just dropped.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: This makes all the difference
body:
Winning a race like this takes serious planning.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1343&source=&t=1&akid=3186%2E124072%2EDV2LL9) | | | |
---
Peter,
I’m writing to you today to ask you to become a weekly donor to my campaign here in North Carolina. You haven’t chipped in yet, but if you want to flip this seat and the Senate in November, this is the most strategic donation you can make to ensure that happens.
If that’s all you need to hear, you can use this link to donate: [**_https:/ /secure.actblue.com/donate_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/17620?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1343&amount=5&t=8&akid=3186%2E124072%2EDV2LL9)
Otherwise, let me explain why these weekly contributions matter so much.
We’re less than 45 days out from the start of early voting in North Carolina, and we have big fundraising goals to hit before then so we can reach as many voters as possible and get them to the polls.
My team and I sit down each week to make sure we’re on track – _and_ to make huge budget decisions for the week ahead – and when we fall short, we have to pull back on things like our critical voter contact and organizing efforts. **The things that win elections.**
Knowing that we have a steady stream of weekly donations coming in from our top grassroots donors makes a real difference. It gives us the flexibility to plan accordingly and withstand whatever my Trump-backed opponent, Michael Whatley, throws our way.
**And, Peter, to be transparent, your first gift – in the form of a weekly donation – is urgently needed.**
Right now, the GOP is doubling down on its attacks against me. Super PACs are spending nearly $100 million so far to push out attack TV ads that lie about me. President Trump and MAGA loyalist Stephen Miller are smearing me on social media and Fox News.
They’re all coming after me because experts say North Carolina will decide control of the Senate. Now, my lead is shrinking: A new poll shows this race statistically tied.
**I’m relying on a surge of grassroots support to pull ahead, so if you’ve been waiting for the best time to have the biggest impact on our fight, today is the day.**
[**_Will you start a weekly donation of $5, or whatever amount is meaningful to you, from now until Election Day? Together, I know we can win in North Carolina and take back the Senate._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/17620?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1343&amount=5&t=9&akid=3186%2E124072%2EDV2LL9)

---
I appreciate all you’re doing to help power this grassroots movement. Thank you!
Roy Cooper

custom_fields.mailing_source_code %}&amounts=amounts) Peter,

When I first ran for the Minneapolis School Board, I didn’t think we would win. I thought we would stand up for our community and share important concerns.

But I never imagined how many of my neighbors shared those concerns.

While I was running, I met an old woman at a public housing complex for urban native communities.

She was selling frybread – and had a little Folgers coffee can where everyone was putting in $5. After we spoke, she took $5 out, put it in my hand, and wrapped her finger around it.

She told me: “My girl, we’re so proud of you.”

**That $5 meant more to me than a giant check from someone I knew could afford it.**

I’m running for Senate to give back to the communities that have given me so much. I want to be the voice for Minnesota families in Washington. And folks know it.

This is a grassroots campaign, powered by normal Minnesota families chipping in $5 or $10 at a time.

Since our launch, our average contribution has been just $25. Some people give more, some people give less. But I am honored and humbled by every donation. body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2803%2E5691347%2EuIhSXH)

Peter, we have to be honest with you.
When Jon first launched his reelection campaign, we weren’t sure what to expect.
Hundreds of thousands of people chipped in to support him in his last Senate race, and we won an incredible victory alongside Rev. Warnock, but that was a long time ago, and a lot has changed since then.
But WOW, Peter! Throughout this campaign, it has been absolutely _incredible_ to see how many people are chipping in again, and how many are getting involved for the first time.
Many people give because they understand that winning back the Senate is our last chance to stop a complete MAGA takeover. Others, because they see the good work Jon is doing in the Senate fighting for Georgians, and want to see that work continue.
No matter your reason for getting involved, _thank you_. But we have to ask you for more today.
We can win this race in a landslide and send an _unmissable_ message to Trump and MAGA, but the ONLY way it’s possible, the ONLY way Jon’s going to have the resources to fight back against the Super PACs and dark money groups... is with our support, Peter.
[**So we’re humbly asking: Can you PLEASE make a donation today — of any amount that feels right to you?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-sep26.MEWcSy&refcode=em260902-3-t&utm_campaign=em260902-3-t&t=2&akid=2803%2E5691347%2EuIhSXH)
Our average online donation is about $30. Many first-time donors give just $5 or $10. The most important thing isn’t the amount of the donation, it’s that you’re chipping in to support Jon and being a part of this movement.
When we win this race in November, please know that your support in moments like this is what made it possible.

| | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. **Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him.** The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away.[**Will you help Sgt. Duran fight for his freedom?**](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=f665c42414284277be8b8d2bcb4539ef&_e=YeCvDxPY-TkI2oLutLcmyMFjYuJ61XzbU8If6rWuYlf7i1c6qWXitvgvZTjmsmJArZxng_Un1MhOg2GrPALmmC5cc-ueUE6yNqgntKMkIHGiSmK0a7N1sDlzwA-jC_B_2UsMs_CwL4Cw1yNgT-Zx6PIV9poHP91pmzzSVtvYqJKiRo8ZshngdTkDK1zhZ4qrJVu7fgzrjZIWoy3l96me_dBxK4q01mfcTekBAP5a6QlKQyBg4ovN87KyQKz7qy2Sb_2KOjVbcHO3xgtSGjmeuzMjR4cYNWRTYBJTp3LABeblgKyZBgY4SlDGBNZgXEYP89ob4Z71eYooiAoWSistTKvDGLE8zgTC3M4Rm__-1l7NP3uTewT05a6OacqAVYlnjk9Ie6onEpmlJGRoAO5Yv5vEx52jcig6JSuyZFdyCcss6BLlazZLR4TUsWOPQ1YYJfXXaGPJjbJ1aj6mL7fuk4Au_tkXi2C6FmebEitEKJwehp4tuNQprTZlZ8q-Hue4j1gJ9AUYtjM6-U_x0sW5BM8xnJ-gWBV8zW1sZlqoBErHIwvd3CXfCDg0L7MY1G6ZoyKo7m1UH6mmtVXjf9Qw7yOfK1UDsyPQbHd8Ul_HZhMsm91Gzn6NkQ9cy0xNG5EcJwi2VhU0mptq2kL4an9wLavZj9KS8z7mtQws3AUX-FgWx1-ZxYYaKF1loo0YZ02a) The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. clean_body: Convicted because of a cooler | | | | | | Dear Fellow American,This officer was just convicted of manslaughter for trying to stop a fleeing criminal with non-lethal force. Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. Now he's fighting for his own freedom – All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx. | | | | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him. The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away. The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. Duran and helping fund his appeal.But legal battles like this are long, difficult, and incredibly expensive.And while Erik fights for his freedom, his wife and children are left carrying the burden alongside him. They’re not only facing the reality of their husband and father spending the next 9 years in prison.Their own lives have been threatened because of this case. That's why I’m asking for your help today. spent 15 years protecting others. Now he needs people like you standing behind him. you for standing with Sgt. Duran. Sincerely, | | | Jason Johnson, President Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. To read more about our mission or the other Law Enforcement officers we're defending, please visit www.leldf.org. Giuliani filed a motion asking the U.S. District Court for the
Southern District of New York to unseal materials related to two
search warrants targeting Giuliani’s electronic information and
telephone records. The warrants authorized the government to seize and
search Giuliani’s iCloud account and obtain prospective and
historical location information for two telephone numbers assigned to
him (In re Search Warrants Executed on April 28, 2021 (No. 21-mc-00425
(JPO))).

Sorry, Hillary. I didn't vote for you.
Solely being a woman isn't a qualification for leadership.
Fellow American, I've had some stuff on my mind and it feels really good to get it off my chest.
I'm sure you know by now that I've recently walked away from a career I loved. Plenty of people call me crazy for it. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line._
_Especially in my beloved Minnesota.
Right now, parents who speak up are being called transphobes. Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet. And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
It's terrible.
That's why I've taken a huge leap of faith. I want my daughter and every young girl and boy across the country to know this:
1) You earn your place 2) You think for yourself 3) You never let anyone put you in a box
That's exactly what I'm fighting for.
It's not rocket science. GIRLS' sports are for GIRLS.
And if you are to remember one thing about me let it be this: I will not apologize for taking a stand. At the end of the day, if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, I've done my job.
Now, the contingent of people on the radical Left who have been pushing this ideology tirelessly on us will stop at absolutely nothing.
Whether I face Peggy Flanagan or Angie Craig, I'm going up against a far-Left, extremist who will vote to allow boys competing against girls in sports, block voter ID requirements, open up our borders, raise your taxes, and sabotage anything the President wants to do.

I'm far from a career politician. My campaign is focused on honesty, common sense, stopping fraud, and doing the small things right.
That's why we need to win. Failure here is not an option.
And without your help, Fellow American... we will never cut through the far Left's propaganda machine to get our message out.

Fellow American, I've had some stuff on my mind and it feels really good to get it off my chest. I'm sure you know by now that I've recently walked away from a career I loved. Plenty of people call me crazy for it. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line. Especially in my beloved Minnesota. Right now, parents who speak up are being called transphobes. Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet. And women's groups are nowhere to be found. It's terrible. That's why I've taken a huge leap of faith. I want my daughter and every young girl and boy across the country to know this: 1) You earn your place 2) You think for yourself 3) You never let anyone put you in a box That's exactly what I'm fighting for. It's not rocket science. GIRLS' sports are for GIRLS. And if you are to remember one thing about me let it be this: I will not apologize for taking a stand. At the end of the day, if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, I've done my job. Now, the contingent of people on the radical Left who have been pushing this ideology tirelessly on us will stop at absolutely nothing. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: I need to tell you what I saw in Georgia
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Stewart Detention Center is a failure of the promise of America — what I witnessed there was horrific.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260902-6677-footer&t=1&akid=6677%2E420207%2EmiED_Y)
Peter,
My tour of the Stewart Detention Center in Georgia left me horrified.
Stewart Detention Center is one of the largest private immigration facilities in the country, run by CoreCivic — **a for-profit prison company that has built a business off of human misery for years.**
The facility is over capacity by hundreds, and has been since Trump returned to office. The conditions inside reflect it:
**❌ Black water coming out of the taps.
❌ Limited access to medical care.
❌ Verbal abuse from staff.
❌ Poor living conditions.
**
ICE officials claim these are not problems within Stewart, but I heard stories from detainees who are so desperate for clean, drinkable water that they’re spending money to buy bottled water from the commissary instead. Stories of medical malpractice and abuse. Stories of unhygienic, unlivable, and undignified conditions.
**Some people are being detained in these terrible conditions for a year, even two years.**
They are not the “worst of the worst.” 73% of those in immigration detention have no criminal record. And the vast majority of remaining 27% have minor convictions like traffic tickets. This is according to ICE’s own records. They deserve dignity and respect, and are instead worried every single day about their own survival, and the family members they left behind.
**This is what our tax dollars are funding, Peter. $150 a day to hold people who in an overwhelming number of cases, should never have been detained in the first place.**
Every person inside of these detention centers deserves their dignity and humanity to be seen and respected. Instead, people are being starved of their basic needs while a corporation is making hundreds of millions of dollars on human suffering, fueled by this administration’s campaign of cruelty.
I refuse to accept this level of cruelty as normal.
**Stewart is a failure of the promise of America.** I won’t stop working until the doors of this facility are shut, and all private, for-profit detention centers are shut down for good.
[**If you’re able, please pitch in $3 today or whatever you can to help me keep fighting for the dignity and rights of every person in this country.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260902.c8gYyD&refcode=em20260902-6677&amount=3&t=2&akid=6677%2E420207%2EmiED_Y)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260902.c8gYyD&amount=3&refcode=em20260902-6677&t=21&akid=6677%2E420207%2EmiED_Y)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

The country is at an inflection point, and we need someone who can meet the moment. Every day, democracy is under assault by the Trump administration and MAGA movement. Senator Wiener has spent the year fighting back; writing laws to force ICE agents to take off their masks, giving Californians the ability to sue ICE when they violate your constitutional rights, and restoring catastrophic cuts to our scientific community.

We can’t afford to send someone to Washington who doesn’t have the backbone and experience to take on MAGA on day one. Representing San Francisco in Congress is an enormous responsibility, and I know Scott is up to the challenge.
-Josh

name: Darline Graham
subject: A promise made a long time ago
body:
Some moments you never forget. This was one of them. |
---

Fellow Patriot,

There's a moment I've never forgotten.

I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next.

[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=468b4edeb6864e80a4307b376fe8d103&_e=thb9Gtn6XNq6ykNFW_oyH2n5KzrEovTbHxPzlJBNuy_xkaB-4DZtJy8G5EYW3mi-AXCfpJU8kpuCxs8z0wJBred6z2JjrmXGDRUe6y36u9W_iI1TDWR6fjvkZtyt4JVthOUP9BF4i2CQR4mCI15_tbebJC_iSN4sAhZ-WqzU85zCaqzMVBcNZky6zIM4qBXd6UMo_6JyKHIKlpIvaJyvoPMDjWXmGZHyiS2IcxPKbttxKcrIEvdTL24vC1JOxFVnCv5RZ6hlTZcp26xpwn8YuvNDsenBoGJ3ZWfeSm0iKNV6euZsKBKTQJZNcsWYfXuKJuQXn78wZpfeXX43AMp8M-IE2ySMjGvHPnwXrudAoMWTMpwoZwLELZ4YS8QMt8wQL9PI-t-IrhfBgetOc_oBwk0eTls3-djhvS3LFODmmsnV0hwc-oqbcj9K8I-bbXkgFjZdrkiLkPUr4vEeAR2XS66sRq5hPqmuryWvHWfRvusQwzVMj11jdhh2SZ7fShsD7G6EqC7vfksj_qxjMJnkBZF8Y_QudplOgPxcGEUI1qyq86UNpNaxGpS_DWAWIYIetxTEK3IzU33yViudm6oI_I_bu1B2JXRrUQdnEU7h8bb8IX5dF-CNmHO-SSCaCgnDlDAORGJFs8UZqXVpnIPMfkQ2OSNre9uLv2ilV91BhRjQ19eMCSPMaoofmO3qlt-s1umXzVEN8lpBXBv7KWTlrQ%3D%3D)
My brother Lindsey figured it out.

He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did.

Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night.

Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did.

After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything.

You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? _Because he knew who was counting on him._

It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder.

These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner.

**The radical left in this country today:** they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good.

I'm here to tell you it isn't.

clean_body: Some moments you never forget. This was one of them. | Fellow Patriot, There's a moment I've never forgotten. I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next. My brother Lindsey figured it out. He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did. Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night. Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did. After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything. You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? Because he knew who was counting on him. It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder. These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner. The radical left in this country today: they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good. I'm here to tell you it isn't. The legacy my brother built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did every single day for the great people of South Carolina. I am starting this General Election behind financially. All those years ago, he promised me things would be okay. Now, it's my turn to pick up where he left off and make sure the people he loved, South Carolinians from the Grand Strand to the Golden Corner, are okay. I can't let him down. That's why, when President Trump asked me to run, I answered the call. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.
